records.name: The Agricultural Conservation Easement Program (ACEP)
records.problem: Protects the agricultural viability and related conservation values of eligible land by limiting nonagricultural uses which negatively affect agricultural uses and conservation values, protect grazing uses and related conservation values by restoring or conserving eligible grazing land, and protecting and restoring and enhancing wetlands on eligible land.
records.eligibility: Agricultural Land Easements (ALE) are available for cropland, rangeland, grassland, pastureland, and nonindustrial private forest land associated with an agricultural operation. Wetland Reserve Easements (WRE) are available for farmed or converted wetlands that were previously altered for agricultural production and can be successfully and cost-effectively restored
records.requirements: ACEP is a voluntary conservation easement program with two components: Agricultural Land Easements (ALE) and Wetland Reserve Easements (WRE). NRCS enters into agreements with eligible entities for ALE and purchase agreements with eligible private landowners or American Indian tribes for WRE. Applications are accepted year-round and funding is awarded through a competitive ranking process.
records.notes: Landowners retain private ownership while agreeing to maintain specific land uses. Easements are voluntary, monitored annually for compliance, do not require public access, and may provide financial and technical assistance. WRE easements include permanent, 30-year, term easements, and 30-year contracts for Tribal lands

records.name: ACEP_ Agricultural Land Easements (ALE)
records.problem: Loss of agricultural land, conversion of agricultural land to non-agricultural uses, fragmentation of working lands, and loss of conservation values.
records.eligibility: Eligible land includes private or Tribal agricultural land, cropland, rangeland, grassland, pastureland, and nonindustrial private forest land associated with an agricultural operation. Land must also meet at least one of the following eligibility criteria: (1) protect Prime, Unique, or Other productive soils; (2) protect grazing uses and related conservation values; (3) contain historical or archaeological resources; or (4) further a state or local policy consistent with the purposes of ACEP-ALE. Eligible partners include American Indian tribes, state and local governments, and nongovernmental organizations with farmland or grassland protection programs
records.requirements: NRCS provides financial assistance to eligible partners for purchasing Agricultural Land Easements that protect the agricultural use and conservation values of eligible land. Applications are accepted year-round and awarded through a competitive ranking proces

records.name: ACEP_ Wetland Reserve Easements (WRE)
records.problem: Agricultural Conservation Easement Program provides habitat for migratory waterfowl and other wetland dependent wildlife, including threatened and endangered species; improves water quality by filtering sediments and chemicals; reduces flooding; recharges groundwater; protects biological diversity; and provides opportunities for educational, scientific and limited recreational activities.
records.eligibility:
Owners of privately held land including land that is held by American Indian tribes.
All landowners who meet the adjusted gross income (AGI) limitations, including all members of landowner-legal entities, and those compliant with the Highly Erodible Land and Wetland Conservation provisions of the Food Security Act of 1985.
records.notes: MD guide: [local file reference omitted]

records.name: ACEP_Wetland Reserve Enhancement Partnership (WREP)
records.problem: Wetland degradation, declining water quality, flood vulnerability, loss of wildlife habitat, and degraded wetland functions
records.eligibility: Eligible partners include state and local units of government, Indian Tribes, and nongovernmental organizations. Individual landowners may not submit WREP proposals directly. Interested landowners may apply for enrollment only within an approved WREP project area by submitting Form NRCS-CPA-1200 to NRCS. Eligible lands must meet all ACEP-WRE eligibility requirements, including farmed or converted wetlands that can be successfully and cost-effectively restoredts.
records.requirements: NRCS enters into WREP agreements with eligible partners to leverage financial and technical resources for high-priority wetland protection, restoration, and enhancement projects. Partner contributions must equal at least 15% of the total estimated easement acquisition, restoration implementation, and habitat enhancement costs. All landowner enrollments funded through WREP must comply with ACEP-WRE program and eligibility requirements..
records.practice: Eligible lands may be enrolled under permanent easements, 30-year easements, or 30-year contracts (for acreage owned by Indian Tribes). For enrolled lands, NRCS develops and implements a Wetland Reserve Easement restoration plan to restore, protect, and enhance wetland functions and values. Restoration activities may include habitat enhancement, restoration planning, and implementation through ACEP-WRE easements
records.contacts: Each County has its own Rep: Use this website to find: https://www.nrcs.usda.gov/contact/find-a-service-center?state=24&county=
records.notes: WREP is a special enrollment option under the ACEP Wetland Reserve Easements (WRE) component, rather than a stand-alone easement program. It is designed to leverage partner resources to achieve landscape-scale wetland conservation priorities. NRCS prioritizes proposals that maximize partner contributions, benefit migratory birds and wetland-dependent wildlife, support threatened and endangered species, align with landscape conservation initiatives, and include outreach to underserved agricultural communities

records.name: Regional Conservation Partnership Program (RCPP)
records.problem: Natural resource challenges on agricultural land, including on-farm, watershed, and regional resource concerns; soil health, water quality, wildlife habitat, land health, resource management, sustainable agriculture, and long-term viability of agricultural, grassland, and forestland.
records.eligibility: RCPP is partner-driven. Eligible organizations interested in partnering with NRCS may apply through the RCPP competition. Eligible partner types include nonprofits, for-profit organizations and businesses, agricultural organizations and organizations with a history of working with producers, Native American tribal organizations and governments, institutions of higher education, and soil and water conservation districts. The lead partner submits the application and, if selected, is responsible for collaborating with NRCS to complete the RCPP project. Individual producers cannot submit proposals for RCPP project areas, but farmers, ranchers, forest landowners, producers, landowners, and communities may participate in active RCPP projects. RCPP projects must be carried out on agricultural land, nonindustrial private forest land, or associated land where NRCS determines that eligible conservation activities would help achieve conservation benefits. Eligible conservation activities may also be implemented on public lands when they benefit eligible lands and are included in the approved RCPP project scope.
records.requirements: RCPP projects fall under two categories: RCPP Classic, where projects are implemented through NRCS using NRCS contracts and easements with producers, landowners, and communities in collaboration with project partners; and RCPP Alternative Funding Arrangements (AFA), where NRCS provides funding directly to partners to support conservation activities with producers and reimburses partners for conservation activities done on behalf of producers, landowners, or other entities. Proposed projects must generate conservation benefits by addressing specific natural resource objectives in a state or multi-state area or by addressing one or more primary resource concerns within an NRCS-designated Critical Conservation Area.
records.practice: RCPP may support land management, improvement, and restoration practices; land rentals or payments to producers for actual net loss from land use changes or conservation practices when NRCS payment rates do not cover foregone income; entity-held easements; U.S.-held easements; and public works/watershed improvements through an NRCS-approved watershed plan. A single RCPP project can use any combination of these eligible activity types. Specific practices and activities depend on the approved RCPP project

records.name: Agricultural Management Assistance (AMA)
records.problem: Financial risk on agricultural operations, water management limitations, irrigation infrastructure needs, soil erosion, water quality concerns, and need for conservation practices or production diversification to reduce operational risk.
records.eligibility:
Producers must: Be engaged in livestock or agricultural production.
Have an interest in the farming operation associated with the land being offered for AMA enrollment.
Have control of the land for the term of the proposed contract.
Land Eligibility: Land on which agricultural commodities or livestock are produced, such as cropland, hayland, pastureland, rangeland, and grassland.
Land used for subsistence purposes, private non-industrial forestland, or other land on which agricultural products, livestock, or forest-related goods are produced.
Land on which risk may be mitigated through operation diversification or change in resource conservation practices.
records.requirements: NRCS works with producers to develop an AMA plan of operations. Contracts are for a minimum of one year after completion of the last practice and no more than 10 years. Participants are expected to maintain cost-shared practices for the life of the practice. AMA provides financial assistance up to 75% of the cost of installing conservation practices, and total AMA payments may not exceed $50,000 per participant per fiscal year. Participants are subject to Adjusted Gross Income provisions, and AMA offers additional higher cost-share for historically underserved producers.
records.practice: Producers may construct or improve water management structures or irrigation structures; plant trees for windbreaks or to improve water quality; and mitigate risk through production diversification or resource conservation practices, including soil erosion control, integrated pest management, or transition to organic farming.

records.name: Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP)
records.problem: Natural resource concerns on agricultural operations and nonindustrial private forest land, including soil erosion, water quality, wildlife habitat, drainage/water management, forest health, and disaster/climate-related stressors
records.eligibility: Agricultural producers and non-industrial private forest managers/landowners may apply. Applicant generally must control or own eligible land, have farm records/FSA farm number, comply with AGI payment limits and Highly Erodible Land/Wetland Conservation provisions, and develop an NRCS EQIP plan of operations.

records.name: Conservation Stewardship Program (CSP)
records.problem: Soil quality degradation, soil erosion, water quality concerns, water quantity concerns, air quality concerns, degraded plant resources, degraded animal resources, energy concerns, poor grazing conditions, low crop resiliency, limited wildlife habitat, weather and market volatility, high agricultural input needs, and need to improve existing conservation systems on working lands.
records.eligibility: Applicants may include individuals, legal entities, joint operations, or Indian Tribes. Applicants must own or rent and currently manage land for agricultural or forest production; maintain control of the land for the full five-year CSP contract; have a Social Security Number or Employer Identification Number; have an adjusted gross income below $900,000, except Indian Tribes; and comply with highly erodible land and wetland conservation provisions. CSP applicants must meet the stewardship threshold for at least two priority resource concerns on every land use included in the operation when they apply and agree to meet or exceed the stewardship threshold for at least one additional resource concern by the end of the contract. Eligible lands include private agricultural land, agricultural Indian land, nonindustrial private forest land, farmstead, associated agricultural land, and public land under the applicant’s control and part of the operation. CSP enrolls the entire operation, not just one field or tract.Land must already be actively used for agricultural or forest production. Lands being cleared or prepared for future agricultural production are not eligible until an agricultural operation has been established and crops, food, or fiber have been successfully produced. Applicants should check with the local USDA Service Center before clearing land to avoid violating highly erodible land or wetland conservation requirements, which may affect eligibility for USDA programs
records.requirements: CSP helps agricultural and forest producers build on existing conservation efforts while strengthening their operation. NRCS works one-on-one with producers to evaluate current management systems, identify natural resource problems, develop a conservation plan, and select additional conservation practices, activities, enhancements, or bundles based on the producer’s management objectives. CSP contracts are five years, with the possibility of renewal for another five-year period if the first contract is completed and the renewal application ranks high enough. Contract payments are based on maintaining the existing level of conservation and implementing additional conservation activities.
records.practice: CSP supports conservation practices, conservation activities, enhancements, and bundles that improve conservation performance on working lands. Examples include cover crop management, multi-species cover crop enhancement, deep-rooted cover crops to reduce soil compaction, grazing plans, no-till to reduce erosion, forest management for wildlife habitat, resource-conserving crop rotations, advanced grazing management, and Grassland Conservation Initiative activities for eligible grassland producers.

records.name: Emergency Watershed Protection (EWP)
records.problem: Imminent threats to life and property caused by floods, fires, windstorms, and other natural disasters that impair a watershed; flood damage, streambank erosion, debris in stream channels, damaged drainage facilities, critically eroding lands, damaged levees or structures, and flood-prone properties where structural measures are not cost-effective.
records.eligibility: Public and private landowners are eligible for assistance but must generally be represented by a project sponsor. Eligible sponsors include legal subdivisions of a state, such as a city, county, general improvement district, conservation district, flood and water control district, soil and water conservation district, or any Native American Tribe or Tribal organization. The NRCS website also notes that cities, counties, towns, conservation districts, and federally recognized Native American Tribes or Tribal organizations can serve as sponsors, and that public/private landowners usually apply through a local sponsor
records.requirements: EWP is a recovery program for emergencies created by natural disasters. Projects must reduce threats to life and property, be economically, environmentally, and socially defensible, and be technically sound. All projects must have a project sponsor. NRCS completes a Damage Survey Report to investigate site-specific damage and identify measures needed to protect life and property from additional flooding and soil erosion. NRCS funds only the work necessary to reduce applicable threats; if a sponsor wants a higher level of protection, the sponsor pays the additional upgrade cost
records.practice: EWP may support debris removal from waterways, stream channels, road culverts, and bridges; stabilization or protection of unstable/eroded streambanks; correction of damaged or destroyed drainage facilities; vegetative cover on critically eroding lands; repair of levees and structures; repair of certain conservation practices; wind-borne debris removal; recovery measures for damaged upland sites stripped of protective vegetation by fire or drought; floodplain easements; and, in some cases, buyouts where structural protection is not cost-effective.

records.name: Healthy Forests Reserve Program (HFRP)
records.problem: Forest ecosystem degradation, threatened or endangered species habitat needs, reduced plant and animal biodiversity, need to enhance carbon sequestration/carbon storage, and need to restore, enhance, and protect forestland resources on private or Tribal lands
records.eligibility: Land must be private land or Tribal land that will restore, enhance, or measurably increase the likelihood of recovery of a threatened or endangered species, improve biological diversity, or increase carbon sequestration/carbon storage. Both landowners and tenants can participate in different HFRP components. Applicants must provide proof of land ownership for easement enrollments or 30-year contracts with Tribes. Operators/tenants must provide written concurrence from the landowner for the period of an HFRP restoration agreement.
records.requirements: HFRP is a voluntary program that helps landowners restore, enhance, and protect forestland resources through easements, 30-year contracts, and 10-year cost-share agreements. For all HFRP easements, contracts, and 10-year restoration agreements, NRCS develops an HFRP restoration plan. The plan must specify how the enrolled land will be restored, protected, enhanced, maintained, and managed to accomplish program goals. NRCS must confer with the program participant and with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and National Marine Fisheries Service, as appropriate.
records.practice: Land management practices, vegetative treatments, structural practices and measures, carbon sequestration practices, biodiversity improvement practices, and other practices or measures needed to restore and enhance habitat for threatened, endangered, candidate, state-listed, or other priority species

records.name: Wetland Mitigation Banking Program (WMBP)
records.problem: Unavoidable wetland impacts from agriculture; difficulty avoiding or mitigating wetland impacts on-site; need for off-site mitigation through wetland mitigation banking credits; need to maintain compliance with USDA wetland conservation provisions; wetland loss or degradation addressed through wetland restoration, creation, or enhancement
records.eligibility: WMBP is a competitive grants program for bank sponsors. A bank sponsor is any individual or entity that develops wetlands for use in wetland mitigation banking. Bank sponsors can compete for NRCS funding to support the costs of developing and establishing a mitigation bank for use by agricultural producers. Agricultural producers are the users of mitigation bank credits: they may buy credits from wetland mitigation banks to compensate for unavoidable wetland impacts at another location
records.requirements: WMBP provides competitive grants to bank sponsors to develop and establish wetland mitigation banks that make credits available for agricultural producers. Bank sponsors are responsible for developing and maintaining the mitigation bank. Producers do not receive grants directly; they may purchase mitigation credits to compensate for unavoidable wetland impacts when avoidance or on-site mitigation is challenging. Wetland banks are established through restoration, creation, or enhancement, and credits are determined by functional wetland assessment
records.practice: Wetland restoration, wetland creation (CPS658), wetland enhancement (CPS659), establishment of wetland mitigation banks, and sale/purchase of wetland mitigation credits.

records.name: Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP)
records.problem: Degraded water quality, soil erosion, wetland degradation, loss of riparian buffers/filter strips, wildlife habitat loss, reduced grassland productivity, air quality concerns, critical invasive species pressure, threatened and endangered species habitat needs, and surface or groundwater conservation needs.
records.agency: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA), in partnership with states, Tribal governments, nonprofit organizations, and private entities
records.eligibility: Eligible land must have a cropping history for four of the previous six years, applicants must meet the $900,000 Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) limitation, and satisfy all applicable CRP eligibility requirements
records.requirements: Land is enrolled through a CREP agreement developed between FSA and partner organizations to address priority conservation objectives on agricultural lands within specific geographic areas. Participation is subject to the terms negotiated under each CREP agreement
records.strategies: Eligible practices may include riparian buffers, filter strips, wetlands, pollinator plantings, conservation forestry, and other partner-approved practices that restore wildlife habitat, improve grassland productivity, enhance water quality, reduce soil erosion, improve air quality, restore wetlands, conserve water, control invasive species, and protect threatened and endangered species. Participants may receive annual rental payments, Sign-up Incentive Payments (SIP), Practice Incentive Payments (PIP), cost-share assistance, and additional negotiated incentives
records.notes: CREP is a component of the Conservation Reserve Program (CRP) and operates as a public-private partnership. Unlike general CRP enrollment, CREP agreements are developed for specific geographic areas and conservation priorities and may provide higher incentive payments and longer contract lengths than other CRP enrollment options

records.name: CREP_ Delaware
records.problem: Environmentally sensitive agricultural land, water-quality degradation, erosion, sediment/nutrient pollution, wildlife habitat loss, and wetlands restoration.
records.eligibility: To be eligible for the program, at least 80% of a producer’s eligible land must be within the Chesapeake Bay, Delaware Bay or Inland Bays watershed. The land must adjoin drainage ditches, streams or other water bodies. For shallow water area practices, land does not have to be adjoining a ditch or stream. This land must be suitable for this practice as determined by NRCS. The land must be in cropland or marginal pastureland, four out of six years, from 2012-2017. The landowner must have owned the land for 12 months (with certain exceptions).

records.name: Conservation Reserve Program (CRP)
records.problem: Environmentally sensitive agricultural land, soil erosion, water runoff and sedimentation, water quality concerns affecting groundwater, lakes, rivers, ponds and streams, wildlife habitat needs, grassland conversion risk, and need for long-term resource-conserving vegetative cover
records.eligibility: A producer must have owned or operated the land for at least 12 months before submitting an offer for continuous CRP, or 12 months before the close of general or grassland signup, unless the new owner acquired the land due to the previous owner’s death, the ownership change occurred because of foreclosure with timely right of redemption, or FSA determines that the land was not acquired for the purpose of placing it in CRP. For continuous and general CRP, eligible cropland must have been planted or considered planted to an agricultural commodity for four of six crop years from 2012 to 2017 and must be physically and legally capable of being planted in a normal manner to an agricultural commodity. For general signup, land must also have a weighted average erosion index of eight or higher, be enrolled in a CRP contract expiring September 30, 2026, or be located in a national or state conservation CRP priority area. Marginal pastureland may also be eligible for continuous signup. Grasslands CRP has different land eligibility requirements.
records.requirements: CRP pays agricultural producers to take environmentally sensitive land out of production and plant long-term conservation cover, such as grasses or trees. These covers help reduce soil erosion, improve water quality, and create wildlife habitat. Participants receive rental payments and cost-share assistance, with contracts usually lasting 10 to 15 years. General CRP offers are ranked based on environmental benefits, including wildlife habitat, water quality, erosion reduction, air quality, long-term conservation value, and cost
records.practice: Long-term, resource-conserving vegetative cover, such as approved grasses or trees; conservation practices for environmentally sensitive land under Continuous CRP; and grassland protection for rangeland, pastureland, and other eligible grasslands under Grasslands CRP.
records.contacts: Each County has its own Rep: Use this website to find: https://www.nrcs.usda.gov/state-offices/new-jersey/news/nrcs-in-new-jersey-announces-2nd-conservation-stewardship-program
records.notes: Enrollment options include General CRP, Continuous CRP, Grassland CRP, State Acres for Wildlife Enhancement (SAFE), Highly Erodible Land Initiative (HELI), Clean Lakes, Estuaries and Rivers Initiative (CLEAR30), Farmable Wetland Program (FWP), Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program (CREP), and the Transition Incentives Program (TIP).

records.name: CRP_ Farmable Wetlands Program (FWP)
records.problem: Degraded farmable wetlands, loss of wetland vegetation, poor water quality, reduced wildlife habitat, soil erosion, and need to control water flow on previously cropped wetland areas.
records.eligibility: Farmers and landowners with land suitable for wetland restoration. The land must have been previously cropped and meet specific criteria for enrollment. Applicants must demonstrate the potential for significant environmental benefits through the implementation of conservation practices.
records.requirements: FWP is part of the Conservation Reserve Program (CRP). It encourages farmers and landowners to restore farmable wetlands and establish conservation practices to improve environmental health. The program targets specific non-floodplain wetlands suitable for restoration. Participants receive annual rental payments, cost-share assistance, and other financial incentives for contracts typically lasting 10 to 15 years
records.practice: Restoration of farmable wetlands; establishment of vegetative cover such as native grasses, trees, and other wetland vegetation; installation of conservation structures to control water flow and improve habitat

records.name: CRP_State Acres for Wildlife Enhancement (SAFE)
records.problem: Wildlife habitat loss, limited food sources for priority wildlife species, threatened and endangered species habitat needs, declining grassland bird and wildlife populations, degraded native grassland habitat, sediment and nutrient runoff, and soil and water health concerns
records.eligibility: SAFE practices are available through CRP continuous signup, so participants must meet applicable CRP eligibility requirements and have eligible land for the SAFE practice offered in their area. SAFE availability depends on state-specific projects and local practice availability. Landowners should check with the local FSA county office for SAFE signup periods and eligible practices in their area
records.requirements: SAFE is a CRP initiative that restores habitat to meet high-priority state wildlife conservation goals. Through SAFE, landowners establish wetlands, grasses, trees, buffers, and longleaf pine to create critical habitat and food sources for priority wildlife species. SAFE practices also help protect soil and water health by reducing sediment and nutrient runoff before they reach waterways. Practices are available through CRP continuous signup and depend on local SAFE project availability.
records.practice:
CP38A - Buffers
CP38B - Wetlands
CP38C - Trees
CP38D - Longleaf Pine
CP38E - Grass

records.name: CRP_Clean Lakes, Estuaries and Rivers (CLEAR) Initiative / CLEAR30 Pilot)
records.problem: Sediment loading, nutrient loading, harmful algal blooms, soil erosion, degraded water quality, limited wildlife habitat, and need for longer-term conservation protection.
records.eligibility: CLEAR: land must be eligible and suitable for one of the listed CLEAR conservation practices, and producers may enroll eligible land through Continuous CRP signup. CLEAR30: eligible land is more specific; it must be cropland or certain marginal pastureland currently enrolled in a Continuous CRP or CREP contract, dedicated to an eligible water quality practice, and expiring on September 30, 2026
records.requirements: CLEAR practices are enrolled through Continuous CRP and must be used to reduce sediment loading, nutrient loading, and harmful algal blooms. Participants must establish and maintain the approved water quality practice for the CRP contract period. For CLEAR, contracts follow the regular CRP structure of 10–15 years. For CLEAR30, participants enter a 30-year CRP contract for eligible expiring Continuous CRP or CREP water quality practices. CLEAR30 land has periodic USDA onsite monitoring, and required maintenance activities are incorporated into the Conservation Plan. Compatible uses such as hunting/fishing, managed timber harvest, or periodic haying and grazing are allowed only if consistent with the Conservation Plan and if they do not degrade water quality or conflict with the purpose of the practice.
records.practice: CP8A Grass Waterways; CP15A Contour Grass Strips; CP15B Contour Grass Strips on Terraces; CP21 Filter Strips; CP21B Denitrifying Bioreactor on Filter Strips; CP21S Saturated Filter Strips; CP22 Riparian Buffer; CP22B Denitrifying Bioreactor on Riparian Buffer; CP22S Saturated Riparian Buffer; CP23 Wetland Restoration; CP23A Wetland Restoration, Non-Flood Plain; CP29 Marginal Pastureland Wildlife Habitat Buffer; CP30 Marginal Pastureland Wetland Buffer; CP31 Bottomland Timber Establishment on Wetlands; CP37 Duck Nesting Habitat; CP43 Prairie Strips

records.name: Alley Cropping
records.problem: Surface water runoff and erosion, wind erosion, excess subsurface water, water table depth, nutrient utilization, wildlife habitat
records.strategies: Trees or shrubs planted in rows with agronomic, horticultural, or forage crops cultivated between rows; examples include wheat, corn, soybeans, hay, sunflowers, medicinal herbs, black walnut, pecan, nut or fruit trees, and short rotation woody crops combined with forage or row crops
records.eligibility: Applies to agricultural land, cropland, and forage systems
records.requirements: Requires consideration of spacing, canopy density, crop rotation, nutrient management, pest management, grazing management, and erosion control

records.name: Amending Soil Properties with Gypsum Products
records.problem: Aluminum toxicity and degraded soil conditions associated with SWI, including poor water infiltration, poor soil aggregate stability, and dissolved phosphorus in surface and ground water (nutrient runoff)
records.strategies: Use of gypsum (calcium sulfate dihydrate) products to improve soil properties; gypsum applied based on soil tests and cation exchange capacity
records.requirements: Requires current soil test, validated gypsum source, chemical analysis documentation, appropriate application rates, and livestock exclusion until gypsum is removed from vegetation by rainfall or irrigation

records.name: Brush Management
records.problem: Undesirable woody vegetation, invasive and noxious plants, soil erosion, sediment, water quality degradation, degraded hydrology, reduced forage accessibility, and excessive fuel loads.
records.strategies: Management or removal of woody (nonherbaceous or succulent) plants using mechanical, chemical, burning, or biological methods; may include grazing animals for biological control
records.eligibility: Applies on all lands except active cropland where removal, reduction, or manipulation of woody plants is desired
records.requirements: Requires brush management plan, monitoring plan, treatment specifications, and compliance with Federal, State, and local laws; follow-up treatments may be necessary
records.notes: May support management of invasive woody vegetation (e.g. Phragmites), degraded coastal vegetation, and fuel loads in SWI-affected areas

records.name: Channel Bed Stabilization
records.problem: Channel bed instability, damaging aggradation or degradation, sediment transport and deposition, altered surface water and groundwater levels in floodplains, riparian areas, and wetlands
records.strategies: Measures used to stabilize the bed or bottom of a channel; may include stabilization structures, vegetation, and sediment management measure
records.eligibility: Existing or newly constructed alluvial or threshold channels undergoing damaging aggradation or degradation
records.requirements: Requires site-specific plan, compliance with local, State, Tribal, and Federal laws, evaluation of channel stability and sediment transport, and operation and maintenance plan with periodic inspections
records.notes: Can support stabilization and sediment management in SWI-affected floodplains, wetlands, riparian areas, and coastal channels

records.name: Clearing and Snagging
records.problem: Reduced stream, flow capacity, ponding and flooding, excessive bank erosion, sediment transported to surface water, and debris impacts to infrastructure
records.strategies: Removal of specified vegetation along streambanks and selective removal of snags, drifts, trees, brush, and other obstructions from natural or improved streams; disturbed areas restored with vegetation, preferably native vegetation from local sources
records.eligibility: Applies to any natural or improved stream where removal of vegetation, trees, brush, and other obstructions is needed to restore flow capacity, reduce erosion, sediment transport, flooding, or debris impacts to infrastructure
records.requirements: Requires permits prior to construction, evaluation of modified flow conditions and stream stability, proper debris disposal, vegetation restoration using native species, invasive species prevention and minimization of disturbance to wetlands and riparian habitats
records.notes: Can support channel flow restoration and erosion reduction in SWI-affected riparian and coastal areas

records.name: Conservation Cover
records.problem: Sediment transport to surface water, water quality degradation (nutrient runoff), poor soil health, soil compaction, and inadequate wildlife and pollinator habitat
records.strategies: Establishing and maintaining permanent vegetative cover; may include diverse mixtures of tree, shrub, grass, forb, legume species and native species
records.eligibility: Applies on most lands needing permanent vegetative cover (does not apply to forage production plantings or critical area plantings)
records.requirements: Requires selection of adapted species, appropriate planting methods and seeding rates, weed control, vegetation establishment and maintenance practices, management practices to protect wildlife habitat and control invasive species, and compliance with National Organic Program (NOP) rules for organic operation
records.notes: Supports revegetation, soil stabilization, and reduction of erosion and nutrient runoff in SWI-affected areas

records.name: Conservation Crop Rotation
records.problem: Saline seeps/salt accumulation in soils, poor soil moisture efficiency, nutrient-related water quality degradation (nutrient runoff), soil erosion, reduced soil health/organic matter, and degraded forage and wildlife habitat
records.strategies: At least two different crops grown over time; may include high-residue crops (e.g., corn or wheat), low-residue crops (e.g., vegetables or soybeans), forage crops, perennial deep-rooted crops, legumes, grasses, broadleaf crops, and cover crops
records.eligibility: Applies to all cropland where at least one annually planted crop is included in the crop rotation
records.requirements: Requires a planned crop sequence with at least two different crops, suitable crop substitutions, crop selection based on soil conditions, salinity, water balance, nutrient uptake, and conservation objectives, and use of biomass/crop residue management to reduce erosion and improve soil health

records.name: Constructed Wetland
records.problem: Nutrient runoff, poor water quality, drainage water contamination, and degraded wetland/waterflow conditions
records.strategies: Artificial wetland ecosystem with hydrophytic vegetation for biological treatment of water; treats wastewater, contaminated runoff, storm water, and drainage water using wetland plants tolerant to nutrients, salts, pesticides, and other contaminants. Invasive and noxious species are not used.
records.eligibility: Applies where treatment or water quality improvement of agricultural wastewater, runoff, drainage water, or other waterflows is needed
records.requirements: Requires structures to control water inflow and outflow, maintenance of appropriate water depths and hydraulic retention time, compliance with discharge permit requirements, use of locally adapted hydrophytic vegetation tolerant to contaminated flows, invasive species prevention, and long-term maintenance

records.name: Contour Buffer Strips
records.problem: Soil erosion, sediment transport, nutrient and pesticide runoff, water quality degradation, and poor water infiltration
records.strategies: Perennial grass strips alternated with cultivated contour-farmed strips; vegetation consists of adapted grasses or mixtures of grasses and legumes
records.eligibility: Applies on all sloping cropland, including orchards, vineyards, and nut crops
records.requirements: Requires permanent vegetative buffer strips with adapted grasses, legumes, or forb mixtures, stable outlets for runoff flow, contour-based strip layout, minimum strip widths and stem density requirements, erosion and sediment control, and maintenance of at least 95% vegetative ground cover
records.notes: Effectiveness depends on slope, soil type, crop type, strip width, management, and climatic conditions; more difficult to establish on undulating or rolling topography

records.name: Cover Crop
records.problem: Soil erosion, reduced soil organic matter, poor soil aggregate stability, nutrient-related water quality degradation (nutrient runoff), poor moisture management, and soil compaction
records.strategies: Grasses, legumes, and other forbs planted for seasonal vegetative cover
records.eligibility: Applies on all lands requiring seasonal vegetative cover for natural resource protection or improvement
records.requirements: Requires adapted species selection, appropriate seeding rates and planting dates, compatible crop rotation and management practices, weed control, moisture management, cover crop termination planning, and compliance with National Organic Program (NOP) rules for organic systems
records.notes: Cover crop termination timing should follow NRCS/RMA termination guidelines ( https://www.nrcs.usda.gov/sites/default/files/2023-03/cover-crops-termination-guidelines-designed-v4-2019-updated.pdf)

records.name: Critical Area Planting
records.problem: High soil erosion rates, unstable streambanks and shorelines, degraded riparian areas, and disturbed or degraded lands
records.strategies: Permanent vegetation establishes on critical erosion areas using adapted grasses, trees, shrubs and vines
records.eligibility: Applies on highly disturbed or degraded areas, including mined lands, urban restoration sites, construction areas, disaster-affected areas, eroded streambanks, shorelines
records.requirements: Requires site investigation and preparation, adapted species selection, seedbed preparation, planting specifications and timing, soil amendments and mulching when necessary, vegetation establishment methods and erosion stabilization measures
records.notes: Supports stabilization of streambanks, shorelines, riparian areas, dunes, slopes, and other disturbed landscapes

records.name: Deep Tillage
records.problem: Soil compaction, restrictive soil layers, flood overwash deposits, and adverse soil physical or chemical conditions
records.strategies: Deep tillage below normal tillage depth to fracture restrictive soil layers or mix overwash and deposited materials in the root zone
records.eligibility: Lands with compacted layers, restrictive hardpans, or overwash/deposits from erosion or flooding that inhibit plant growth
records.requirements: Requires deep tillage under appropriate soil moisture conditions, operation below restrictive layers, proper equipment and tillage depth selection, and evaluation of soil conditions to avoid bringing unfavorable materials (e.g., high Na or gypsum layers) to the surface

records.name: Dike and Levee
records.problem: Flooding risk, uncontrolled water levels, shoreline and embankment erosion, and water management needs in coastal or low-lying areas
records.strategies: Wetland dikes or flood control levees used to retain or exclude water from the landscape
records.eligibility: Applies where flooding threatens land or property, or where water-level management is needed for wetlands, habitat management, irrigation, drainage water management or crop production
records.requirements: Requires compliance with Federal, State, Tribal, and local regulations; hazard-based design and classification; geologic and site investigations; groundwater and surface water considerations; seepage, drainage, and erosion control; slope protection and vegetative cover establishment; water control structures; and long-term inspection and maintenance plans
records.notes: Design criteria depend on hazard class (risk classification based on potential damage and flood risk), protected property/crop value, and threat to human life.                                                -Planning should also consider impacts on groundwater and surface water patterns, adjacent properties, wetlands and  wildlife habitat.

records.name: Diversion
records.problem: Surface runoff, erosion, sediment accumulation, seepage problems, and water management issues in sloping or disturbed areas
records.strategies: Channels constructed across slopes with a supporting ridge used to intercept, collect, redirect, store, or safely dispose of excess surface and shallow subsurface water; channels are commonly vegetated and may use gravel, concrete, or similar lining materials for erosion protection
records.eligibility: Applies to all land uses where soils and topography allow construction of a diversion with a suitable outlet.
records.requirements: Requires stable outlet design; channel stability and capacity analysis; sediment and erosion control; vegetative establishment or channel lining; appropriate ridge and side-slope design; and long-term inspection and maintenance plans

records.name: Drainage Water Management
records.problem: Poor drainage control, nutrient, pathogen, and pesticide loading, high water tables, poor soil moisture management, and oxidation of organic soils
records.strategies: Management of drainage volume and water table elevation by regulating flow from surface or subsurface agricultural drainage systems
records.eligibility: Applies to agricultural lands with drainage systems that can be adapted to manage drainage volume and water table elevation; suitable for relatively flat or gently sloping areas with high natural water tables
records.requirements: Requires management of drainage discharges and outlet elevations using water-control structures or pumps; development of management calendars and monitoring plans; monitoring of water table and control zones; compliance with Federal, State, Tribal, and local regulations; and operation strategies that minimize nutrient loading, maintain crop root zone conditions, and prevent adverse impacts to surrounding properties or drainage systems
records.notes: - Does not apply to irrigation water management or seasonal inundation from surface runoff  - This practice can be applied to saline or sodic soil conditions, but special considerations related to salinity management, drainage, leaching, soil permeability, and crop tolerance are required to maintain soil productivity and minimize environmental impacts.

records.name: Early Successional Habitat Development/Management
records.problem: Loss of early successional habitat and reduced wildlife habitat diversity
records.strategies: Management of plant succession to develop and maintain early successional habitat for wildlife and natural communities
records.eligibility: Applies on all lands suitable for desired wildlife and plant species
records.requirements: Requires use of regionally adapted plant materials, invasive species control, wildlife-sensitive timing of management activities, minimization of soil disturbance and periodic disturbance or vegetation management to maintain habitat conditions

records.name: Field Border
records.problem: Erosion, sediment transport, nutrient runoff and degraded water quality
records.strategies: Permanent strips of grasses, legumes, forbs, and/or shrubs
records.eligibility: Applies to cropland and pasture fields
records.requirements: Requires use of adapted permanent vegetation; erosion and runoff control design; invasive species management; wildlife-sensitive management activities; sediment and concentrated flow control;

records.name: Field Operations Emissions Reduction
records.problem: Particulate matter emissions, wind erosion, and air quality impacts from cropland field operations
records.strategies: Adjustment of field operations and technologies to reduce particulate matter and nitrogen oxide emissions
records.eligibility: Apllies to cropland
records.requirements: Requires documented reduction in annual emissions from the current system through practices such as combined tillage operations, reduced field passes, precision guidance systems, alternative equipment technologies, timing modifications, and low-dust crop management practices

records.name: Filter Strip
records.problem: Sediment transport, nutrient and contaminant runoff and degraded water quality from overland flow
records.strategies: Permanent strips of herbaceous vegetation ( e.g. grasses, legumes)
records.eligibility: Applies where sensitive areas require protection from runoff contaminants and sediment
records.requirements: Requires uniform sheet flow into the filter strip; dispersion of concentrated flow before entering the strip; appropriate slope and runoff design; establishment and maintenance of permanent herbaceous vegetation; and protection of filter strips from livestock and equipment traffic
records.notes: Filter strips are commonly located between agricultural fields and environmentally sensitive areas such as streams, lake

records.name: Forage Harvest Management
records.problem: Nutrient imbalances, soil compaction, reduced forage quality, and pest pressure from poorly timed or excessive forage removal
records.strategies: Timely cutting and removal of forage crops (e.g. grasses, legumes) as hay, silage or green-chop
records.eligibility: Applies to all lands uses where forage is machine harvested
records.requirements: Requires following State extension recommendations (when available) for harvest timing based on plant maturity, target moisture content, stubble height, length of cut, harvest interval, equipment calibration, pest control, and soil compaction prevention measures

records.name: Forest Farming
records.problem: Reduced plant/tree community diversity, low soil organic matter and degraded terrestrial habitat
records.strategies: Managing or establishing stands of trees or shrubs with compatible understory crops or nontimber forest products (e.g. foliage, mushrooms, berries, roots, nuts, etc.)
records.eligibility: On all lands where trees, shrubs, and woody or nonwoody crops can be grown in combination. This practice does not apply to land that is grazed

records.name: Forest Stand Improvement
records.problem: Poor forest health and productivity, undesirable forest structure and composition,forest pest pressure, wildfire hazard, moisture stress, runoff and erosion risks and inefficient precipitation management
records.strategies: Manipulation of tree and shrub species composition, structure, or density to achieve desired forest conditions
records.eligibility:
Applies on all forestland where manipulation of vegetation
is needed
records.requirements: Requires use of appropriate silvicultural techniques; identification and retention of preferred tree and understory species; management of stand spacing and density; protection of water quality and hydrologic conditions; minimization of rutting, compaction, and soil erosion; woody debris and wildfire hazard management; and timing of activities to minimize impacts on wildlife, fish, and pollinators

records.name: Forest Trails and Landings
records.problem: Soil erosion, soil rutting, compaction, hydrologic disturbance, water quality degradation, stream and riparian damage, and habitat fragmentation caused by unmanaged forest access routes
records.strategies: Creation and management of temporary or seasonal forest access routes, paths, or cleared areas.
records.eligibility: Applies on forest land requiring temporary access to facilitate conservation activities
records.requirements: Requires appropriate trail and landing size, gradient, number, and location; avoidance of poorly suited soils, wetlands, riparian areas, and sensitive habitats; minimization of erosion, compaction, concentrated flow, sedimentation, hydrologic modification, and stream damage; integration of drainage and erosion-control measures; stabilization of disturbed areas; invasive species prevention and compliance with State forestry best management practices

records.name: Grassed Waterway
records.problem: Concentrated surface runoff, gully formation, soil erosion, sediment transport, flooding, and degraded downstream water quality
records.strategies: Grasses, tall bunch grasses, perennial forbs, legumes, and flowering plants used for runoff stabilization and habitat improvement
records.eligibility: Applies where additional water conveyance capacity and vegetative protection are needed to prevent erosion and improve runoff water quality from concentrated surface flow
records.requirements: Requires stable channel and runoff-capacity design; establishment of suitable vegetation with adequate density and vigor; erosion, drainage, and sediment control measures; stable outlets; protection from livestock and equipment damage; and maintenance of vegetative cover and channel stability
records.notes: This practice has a minimum expected life of 10 years

records.name: Hedgerow Planting
records.problem: Habitat fragmentation, airborne dust, chemical drift, odor movement, limited wildlife habitat, and reduced carbon storage
records.strategies: Dense perennial linear plantings of woody plants, shrubs, trees, bunch grasses, and pollinator-supporting vegetation
records.eligibility: Applies wherever dense perennial vegetation can achieve habitat, screening, filtering, barrier, or carbon-storage purposes
records.requirements: Requires sufficient hedgerow width and vertical structure; selection of site-adapted and pest-resistant species; protection from grazing, browsing, trampling, pesticide drift, and invasive vegetation; establishment of woody plants and/or perennial bunch grasses depending on conservation purpose; and maintenance of habitat, screening, or filtering functions

records.name: Mulching
records.problem: Soil erosion, high runoff, soil moisture loss, inefficient irrigation water use, bank erosion, declining soil organic matter and reduced plant productivity
records.strategies: Application of plant residues, grain straw, grass hay, wood chips, bark, shavings, gravel, synthetic mulch, or other suitable materials to the soil surface
records.eligibility: Applies on lands subject to erosion and high runoff requiring additional surface protection
records.requirements: Requires selection of mulch materials appropriate for site conditions and conservation purpose; soil surface preparation; even mulch application and anchoring; erosion and runoff protection measures; compliance with manufacturer specifications for synthetic mulches; maintenance of minimum mulch cover or thickness standards; and proper removal or management of synthetic mulch materials

records.name: Nutrient Management
records.problem: Excess nutrients in surface and groundwater, nutrient losses through runoff or leaching, reduced soil organic matter, nutrient imbalances
records.strategies: Management of nutrient source, rate, timing, and placement for fertilizers, manure, compost, biosolids, crop residues, irrigation water, and other nutrient sources
records.eligibility: Applies to all fields where plant nutrients and soil amendments are applied
records.requirements: Requires a nutrient management plan for N, P, K; soil testing and nutrient risk assessments; implementation of the 4Rs (right source, right rate, right time, right place); nutrient applications based on crop needs and soil conditions; protection of surface and groundwater; periodic plan review and updates; maintenance of records for at least 5 years; and compliance with national, State, and local water quality regulations
records.notes: In areas where salinity is a concern, nutrient sources should be selected to limit soil salt buildup and salt concentrations should be monitored when manure is applied.

records.name: Open Channel
records.problem: Flooding, drainage limitations, water management needs, and protection or enhancement of wildlife habitat
records.strategies: Construction, improvement or restoration of natural or artificial open channels for water conveyance
records.eligibility: Applies to the construction of open channels or modifications of existing streams or ditches with drainage areas exceeding one (1) mi² (1.6 km²)
records.requirements: Requires channel capacity and hydraulic design based on expected flow conditiions; maintenance of channel stability; erosion and sediment control; use of vegetation, riprap, linings or structures where needed; protection of adjacent properties; evaluation of impacts on drainage infrastructure; establishment of vegetation on disturbed areas; and preparation of operation and maintenance plans with inspection, sediment removal, invasive species control, and vegetation maintenance requirements
records.notes: This practice has a minimum expected life of 15 years and may require reconstruction of damaged areas and revegetation of eroded areas

records.name: Pasture and Hay Planting
records.problem: Reduced forage supply, poor livestock nutrition and health, soil erosion, degraded water quality, degraded air quality, and poor soil health
records.strategies: Perennial herbaceous plants, including cool-season and warm-season grasses, legumes, and broadleaf forage species
records.eligibility: Applies on all lands suitable for the one-time establishment of perennial species for forage production expected to persist for 5 years. Does not apply to annually planted and mechanically harvested food, fiber, or oilseed crops on designated cropland
records.requirements: Requires species selection based on climate, soil conditions (including salinity, drainage, flooding, fertility level, pH,and ponding), intended use, compatibility, and pest resistance; compliance with recommended planting rates, methods, and dates (obtained from the NRCS Palnt Materials Program); use of quality seed and planting materials; soil testing and nutrient amendments; adequate soil moisture for establishment; and exclusion of livestock until stands are fully established

records.name: Pond
records.problem: Need for water storage,erosion control, flow detention and water quality improvement
records.strategies: Water impoundments constructed as embankment ponds, excavated ponds, or a combination of both for water storage and managemen
records.eligibility: Applies to all excavated ponds and low-hazard embankment ponds where dam failure would not result in loss of life, damage to homes, commercial or industrial buildings, major highways, railroads, or interruption of public utilities; storage × effective dam height must be less than 3,000 acre-feet² and effective dam height must be 35 ft or less
records.requirements: Requires compliance with Federal, State, and local laws; adequate water supply and suitable water quality; sediment storage capacity or periodic cleanout; erosion protection within the drainage area; safe spillway and runoff conveyance design; establishment of vegetation on disturbed areas; and periodic inspection, sediment removal, vegetation maintenance, and repair of damaged components

records.name: Prescribed Burning
records.problem: Undesirable vegetation, pest, pathogen and disease pressure, wildfire hazards from biomass accumulation, degraded wildlife habitat, reduced plant productivity, forage imbalance, and poor soil health
records.strategies: Planned fire applied to a predetermined area
records.eligibility: Applies on all lands as appropriate
records.requirements: Requires a prescribed burn plan that includes burn area description, preburn vegetation assessment, resource management objectives, required weather conditions, notification procedures, preburn preparation, equipment and personnel assignments, safety requirements, firing sequence, ignition methods, smoke management practices, approval signatures, and postburn evaluation criteria

records.name: Prescribed Grazing
records.problem: Poor forage quantity and quality, sediment and nutrient transport, runoff, soil compaction, groundwater depletion, poor soil health, soil erosion, degraded wildlife habitat, wildfire fuel accumulation, and invasive plant pressure
records.strategies: Management of vegetation with grazing and browsing animals
records.eligibility: Applies on all lands where grazing and/or browsing animals are managed
records.requirements: Requires a grazing management plan that includes management objectives, grazing unit maps, forage inventory, livestock forage demand assessment, feed and forage balance, grazing strategy defining intensity, timing, duration, and frequency of grazing, contingency planning for episodic events, and monitoring protocols with recordkeeping to support adaptive management decisions

records.name: Recreation Land Improvement and Protection
records.problem: Surface irregularities, slopes, obstructions, or drainage limitations that interfere with planned recreational use; resource damage from recreational land use
records.strategies: Land grading, shaping, drainage improvements, and establishment of vegetation to support recreational land use; may include grasses, forbs, trees, and shrubs adapted to site conditions
records.eligibility: Applies to land areas where surface irregularities, slopes, obstructions, or surface drainage interfere with planned recreational use or where such use requires designed land surfaces
records.requirements: Requires compliance with applicable Federal, State, and local laws and regulations; identification of buried utilities and existing infrastructure prior to construction; obtaining all required permits before project installation; grading and shaping plans; drainage design to manage runoff; vegetation establishment using adapted species; erosion and sediment control measures; stormwater pollution prevention plans and operation and maintenance plans

records.name: Residue and Tillage Management, No-Till
records.problem: Sheet, rill and wind erosion; excessive sediment in surface waters; tillage-induced particulate emissions; low soil organic matter and poor aggregate stability; low plant-available moisture; high energy use; and limited wildlife food and escape cover
records.strategies: Limiting soil disturbance; eliminating full-width soil disturbance between cash crops; uniformly distributing crop residues across the field; maintaining sufficient surface residue to control erosion; and maintaining year-round residue cover where applicable
records.eligibility: Applies to all croplands
records.requirements: Requires no full-width soil disturbance between crop cycles; Soil Tillage Intensity Rating (STIR) ≤ 20; residues must not be burned; crop residues must be uniformly distributed across the field; a positive Soil Condition Index (SCI) rating; maintenance of at least 60% residue cover throughout the year to increase plant-available moisture; erosion control based on approved water and wind erosion prediction tools; and preparation of field-specific specifications documenting residue levels, field operations, STIR value, SCI value, and erosion rates

records.name: Residue and Tillage Management, Reduced Till
records.problem: Soil erosion, excessive sediment in surface waters, particulate emissions from tillage, degraded soil health and organic matter, and inefficient energy use
records.strategies: Management of crop and other plant residue on the soil surface year-round while limiting soil-disturbing activities in systems where fields are tilled prior to planting
records.eligibility: Applies to all croplands
records.requirements: Requires uniform residue distribution; no residue burning (except limited approved sugarcane situations); Soil Tillage Intensity Rating (STIR) ≤ 80; no primary inversion tillage implements; positive Soil Condition Index (SCI > 0); and compliance with erosion and energy-reduction criteria where applicable

records.name: Restoration of Rare or Declining Natural Communities
records.problem: Degraded plant condition; inadequate wildlife habitat; degradation or loss of rare or declining native natural communities.
records.strategies: Restore physical/environmental conditions needed by rare or declining natural communities; replace or add substrate; install natural structural elements; create topographic features or chemical conditions that support restoration of native plant communitie
records.eligibility:
Applied on all lands, including degraded aquatic, terrestrial, or wetland sites, that historically supported a
functional rare or declining (dwindling or imperiled) native plant or animal community

records.name: Riparian Forest Buffer
records.problem: Sediment transport, nutrient transport, pathogen, pesticide and chemical movement to surface and groundwater, degraded riparian habitat, elevated stream temperatures, reduced carbon storage, and degraded riparian plant communities
records.strategies: Existing, naturally regenerated, or planted native, noninvasive trees and shrubs adapted to site soil and hydrologic conditions; species may provide timber, nuts, fruit, florals, browse, nesting habitat, and aesthetic value
records.eligibility: Applies to areas adjacent to permanent or intermittent streams, lakes, ponds, and wetlands where channels and streambanks are sufficiently stable
records.requirements: Requires buffer design with sufficient width, length, density, and connectivity to achieve project objectives; use of native, noninvasive trees and shrubs adapted to site soil, hydrology, saturation, and inundation conditions; use of high-quality plant materials; erosion control within and adjacent to the buffer; site preparation and planting to ensure establishment success; livestock exclusion or control as needed; pest management when necessary; and maintenance of tree and shrub densities sufficient to ensure long-term buffer function

records.name: Riparian Herbaceous Cover
records.problem: Degraded water quality, sediment transport, streambank erosion, loss of riparian habitat, reduced floodplain water storage, loss of pollinator habitat, and disturbed riparian plant communities
records.strategies: Establishment or management of grasses, sedges, rushes, ferns, legumes, and forbs tolerant of intermittent flooding or saturated soils as the dominant vegetation between upland and aquatic habitats
records.eligibility: Applies to areas adjacent to perennial or intermittent watercourses and water bodies where herbaceous vegetation tolerant of flooding or saturated soils is the natural or desired community; channel and streambank stability must be adequate; and the riparian area has been altered from its natural condition
records.requirements: Requires selection of perennial species adapted to site hydrology and saturation conditions; use of native seed sources or planting where natural regeneration is insufficient; protection from haying and grazing during establishment; pest management that minimizes impacts on pollinators; site preparation and planting to ensure survival; and buffer width based on geomorphic conditions and project objectives. Domestic grazing should be deferred for at least two years or until establishment is achieved

records.name: Saline and Sodic Soil Management
records.problem: Salt accumulation in the root zone, salt toxicity limiting plant growth, soil crusting, reduced permeability, poor soil aggregate stability, saline seep recharge and discharge areas, wind erosion from sparsely vegetated saline or sodic soils
records.strategies: Salinity mapping (EC); leaching of salts; salt-tolerant vegetation; salt-tolerant cover crops with fibrous roots; deep-rooted, long-season, or perennial species in saline seep recharge areas; gypsum or other calcium amendments; subsoiling; surface or subsurface drainage; revegetation of saline seep discharge areas with species adapted to excess soil moisture
records.eligibility: Applies to all land uses where salinity, sodicity, saline seeps, or salt-related wind erosion limit soil productivity or plant growth.
records.requirements: Requires soil and water testing (EC, SAR, pH, calcium, magnesium, sodium, sulfate); salinity assessment; leaching plans; drainage improvements where needed; vegetation establishment and weed control; soil amendments based on SAR or ESP test results

records.name: Saturated Buffer
records.problem: Elevated nitrate loading in drainage water; altered wetland hydrology; excess drainage discharge to surface waters
records.strategies: Vegetated riparian buffer with artificially raised water table; minimum 30-ft buffer width; vigorously growing herbaceous vegetation, woody shrubs, trees, or a combination; perforated distribution line installed parallel to the watercourse; water control structure used to divert drainage water into the buffer
records.eligibility: Applies to lands with a subsurface drainage system adaptable to discharge into a vegetated area where soils and topography can maintain a raised water table without adverse effects
records.requirements: Requires a minimum 30-ft vegetated buffer, minimum 0.75% organic carbon in the top 2.5 ft of soil, suitable restrictive layer, water control structure, permanent vegetation establishment, and exclusion of livestock from the buffer are

records.name: Seasonal Water Management for Wildlife
records.problem: Loss of wetland habitat, altered hydrology, lack of seasonal standing water for wildlife, need for refuge habitat during flooding events
records.strategies: Seasonal inundation using dikes, ditches, pumps, flooding, or water control structures; management of water depth, duration, timing, and drawdown; habitat for shorebirds, waterfowl, wading birds, mammals, fish, reptiles, and amphibians
records.eligibility: Applies to lands that can be seasonally inundated using existing or planned water management infrastructure and where adequate water supply and drainage are available
records.requirements: Requires habitat evaluation, adequate water quantity and quality, ability to control inundation and dewatering schedules, maintenance of target water depths, and management of water control structures

records.name: Silvopasture
records.problem: Reduced forage productivity, livestock heat or weather stress, soil erosion, degraded water quality, reduced wildlife habitat, low biological diversity, poor soil quality
records.strategies: Establishment and management of trees, forages, and optionally shrubs on the same acreage; trees may be planted in rows, clumps, or as single trees; forage species compatible with livestock and tree species; diverse seed mixes including native forbs and legumes may be used
records.eligibility: Applies to any area suitable for the desired forages, trees, and livestock
records.requirements: Requires adapted tree and forage species, minimum 10% tree stocking, grazing management, livestock distribution infrastructure, invasive species avoidance, protection from pests, wildlife, livestock, and fire, and maintenance of a forested condition

records.name: Soil Carbon Amendment
records.problem: Poor soil organic matter, poor soil aggregate stability, degraded soil health, reduced soil biological activity, low carbon storage
records.strategies: Application of compost, biochar, and other carbon-based materials derived from plant materials or treated animal byproducts
records.eligibility: Applies to Crop, Pasture, Range, Forest, Associated Agricultural Lands, Developed Land, and Farmstead
records.requirements: Requires soil testing prior to application, laboratory analysis of amendment materials, amendment application rates and timing designed to achieve intended purposes, and compliance with applicable regulations

records.name: Stream Habitat Improvement and Management
records.problem: Impaired stream habitat, degraded riparian areas, reduced floodplain connectivity, poor aquatic habitat conditions, altered stream function
records.strategies: Stream habitat assessment; floodplain and wetland connectivity improvements; riparian vegetation restoration using native plants; aquatic organism passage; backwater and off-channel habitat creation; large wood placement, spawning riffles, boulder complexes, and riparian buffer establishment
records.eligibility: Applies to streams and associated backwaters, floodplains, wetlands, and riparian areas with impaired habitat
records.requirements: Requires site-specific assessment of hydrology, channel morphology, aquatic species, riparian and floodplain conditions, water quality, and habitat limitations; native plant materials should be used to the maximum extent possible; livestock must be managed to sustain stream corridor health

records.name: Streambank and Shoreline Protection
records.problem: Streambank erosion, shoreline erosion, land loss, sediment delivery to downstream waters, degraded riparian habitat, unstable banks, scour of estuarine and stream shorelines
records.strategies: Vegetative or structural measures to stabilize and protect streambanks, shorelines, estuaries, lakes, reservoirs, or excavated channels from scour and erosion; may include revegetation, native grasses, forbs, legumes, shrubs, trees, riprap, gabions, buffer establishment, toe protection, and livestock exclusion
records.eligibility: Applies to streambanks of natural or constructed channels and shorelines of lakes, reservoirs, or estuaries susceptible to erosion
records.requirements: Requires assessment of instability causes, treatments compatible with site conditions, hydraulics, and existing vegetation, revegetation of disturbed areas, protection from livestock during vegetation establishment, and periodic inspection and maintenance of vegetative and structural treatments

records.name: Stripcropping
records.problem: Soil erosion, sediment transport to surface waters, nutrient runoff, pesticide transport, wind erosion, reduced infiltration
records.strategies: Planned rotation of erosion-resistant and erosion-susceptible crops arranged in alternating strips; may include crops, forages, specialty crops, cover crops, and grass/legume forage crops; strips are laid out across slopes or perpendicular to prevailing erosive winds
records.eligibility: Applies to cropland
records.requirements: Requires planned crop rotation with alternating erosion-resistant and erosion-susceptible strips; at least 50% of the rotation must consist of erosion-resistant crops or sediment-trapping cover; minimum of two strips; strip widths based on erosion prediction tools; strip orientation designed to reduce water and/or wind erosion

records.name: Subsurface Drain
records.problem: Shallow water table, saturated soils, ponding, flooding, poor plant health and productivity, poor field trafficability, accumulation of salts in the root zone, livestock stress associated with excessive soil moisture
records.strategies: Subsurface drainage pipes or conduit systems installed below ground to remove or distribute soil water; may include drainage laterals, outlets, filters, envelopes, water control structures, sediment traps, and drainage water management components
records.eligibility: Applies to all land uses where a shallow water table exists or where subsurface drainage can mitigate adverse conditions caused by excessive soil moisture, including salt accumulation in the root zone
records.requirements: Requires site-specific design based on soils, hydrology, land use, water table conditions, outlets, saline or sodic conditions, and proximity to wetlands; wetland evaluation required where applicable; drainage outlets and structures must be protected and maintained

records.name: Surface Drain, Field Ditch
records.problem: Ponding, flooding, excess surface water, shallow subsurface water, poor field drainage, poor trafficability, salt accumulation associated with poor drainage
records.strategies: Graded field ditch designed to intercept, collect, and convey excess surface water, shallow subsurface water, seepage, or irrigation water to a stable outlet; may be used with drainage water management, riparian buffers, filter strips, and fencing
records.eligibility: Applies to fields with low permeability soils, shallow restrictive layers (rock or clay), surface depressions, insufficient slope, excessive runoff or seepage from uplands, or excess irrigation water
records.requirements: Requires adequate outlet, site investigation, wetland determination where applicable, ditch sizing based on soils, topography, hydrology, crops, land use, and saline or sodic conditions; periodic inspection, sediment removal, vegetation management, and livestock control
records.notes: Minimum expected lifespan of 15 years

records.name: Surface Drain, Main or Lateral
records.problem: Ponding, flooding, excess surface water, shallow subsurface water, poor drainage, waterlogged soils
records.strategies: Open drainage ditch constructed to a designed size and grade that receives drainage water from field ditches and subsurface drains and conveys it to a safe outlet
records.eligibility: Applies to agricultural sites with an outlet for drainage water by gravity or pumping; applies to disposal of surface and subsurface drainage water collected primarily by field ditches and subsurface drains
records.requirements: Requires a designed drainage ditch integrated into a drainage system and maintenance throughout the expected lifespan of the practice

records.name: Surface Roughening
records.problem: Wind erosion, wind-blown sediment, bare or sparsely covered soils, soil particle abrasion of crops, airborne dust
records.strategies: Emergency tillage operations that create random soil surface roughness (clods, ridges, rough soil surface) to reduce wind erosion; may include chiseling, skip chiseling, deep tillage, lister/bedder operations, or ridging perpendicular to prevailing winds
records.eligibility: Applies to soils with a surface layer suitable for clod formation and a high potential for wind erosion due to insufficient surface cover
records.requirements: Tillage operations must create sufficient random roughness to achieve at least a 25% reduction in potential erosion rate or wind erosion during the management period; intended as an emergency measure rather than a primary erosion control practice

records.name: Trails and Walkways
records.problem: Soil compaction and erosion caused by concentrated animal, pedestrian, or vehicle traffic; damage to sensitive or wet areas; degraded access to forage, water, shelter, or management areas
records.strategies: Constructed path with a vegetated, earthen, gravel, paved, or other hardened surface to facilitate movement of animals, people, or off-road vehicles; may include vegetated trails, gravel walkways, hardened surfaces, elevated walkways, drainage structures, fencing, gates, bridges, and erosion-control measures
records.eligibility: Applies on all lands where management of animal, human, or off-road vehicle movement is needed
records.requirements: Must be designed for intended use, minimize erosion and impacts to riparian areas and wildlife habitat, provide adequate drainage, and comply with applicable laws and permits; vegetation used on trails must be established according to Critical Area Planting (342) criteria when applicable

records.name: Tree/Shrub Establishment
records.problem: Loss of desirable vegetation, erosion, degraded wildlife habitat, degraded water quality, need for forest cover establishment
records.strategies: Establishment of trees and shrubs through planting seedlings or cuttings, seeding, or promoting natural regeneration; species selection, planting method, spacing, and site preparation vary according to site conditions and management objectives
records.eligibility: Applies on any site capable of growing woody plants
records.requirements: Species must be suited to site conditions and intended purpose; invasive or noxious species are prohibited; planted areas must be protected from insects, disease, competing vegetation, fire, livestock, and wildlife

records.name: Tree/Shrub Pruning
records.problem: Poor tree or shrub health, excessive pest pressure, dense canopy limiting understory growth, wildfire hazards, undesirable plant structure, reduced understory vigor
records.strategies: Removal of selected branches, leaders, or roots from trees and shrubs to improve plant health, vigor, structure, understory conditions, or reduce wildfire hazards; may include crown pruning, root pruning, ladder fuel reduction, and removal of diseased branches
records.eligibility: Applies on any area with trees or shrubs
records.requirements: Use proper pruning methods, timing, and tools; remove only the minimum living biomass necessary; sanitize equipment when reducing pest or disease pressure; time activities to minimize impacts to wildlife, soils, and vegetation; treat woody residue where wildfire hazard reduction is an objective

records.name: Tree/Shrub Site Preparation
records.problem: Poor tree/shrub establishment, competing vegetation, pest and disease pressure, flooding or seasonally high water that limits woody plant establishment, degraded sites requiring revegetation
records.strategies: Site preparation using mechanical treatments, herbicides, prescribed burning, vegetation management, residue management, soil preparation, mineral soil exposure, compaction alleviation, and temporary water management to improve establishment of desired trees and shrubs
records.eligibility: Applies on lands suited to growing woody plants where existing site conditions are not suitable for natural or artificial establishment of desired trees and shrubs
