records.name: Virginia Agricultural Best Management Practices Tax Credit Program
records.problem: Cost of implementing conservation practices addressing erosion, runoff, degraded soil, waste management, stream protection, and nutrient loss.
records.eligibility:
A Virginia taxpayer who incurs costs for an agricultural BMP approved by the local Soil and Water Conservation District.
The practice must be installed on acreage covered by an approved soil conservation plan or an approved resource management plan.
Individuals and qualifying pass-through or business entities may claim the credit when they meet the tax and program requirements.
records.requirements: The applicant must contact the local Soil and Water Conservation District before BMP installation; have an SWCD-approved soil conservation plan for the regular 25% credit or an approved Resource Management Plan for the enhanced 50% credit; implement an eligible BMP approved by the Virginia Soil and Water Conservation Board; meet applicable DCR standards and specifications; complete the practice within the taxable year; document eligible out-of-pocket expenditures; obtain SWCD completion and eligibility certification; and submit Form ABM and supporting documentation to Virginia Tax before claiming the credit.
records.benefit:
Virginia income-tax credit for qualifying, district-certified conservation expenditures. A taxpayer with an approved soil conservation plan may claim 25% of the first $100,000 spent on approved BMPs.
A taxpayer with an approved resource management plan may claim 50% of the first $100,000 spent on approved BMPs.
The aggregate credit may not exceed $75,000, and statewide credits are subject to an annual program cap and first-come, first-served issuance

records.name: Virginia Agricultural BMP Loan Program
records.problem: Large up-front costs for agricultural conservation work; polluted runoff; erosion; nutrient, manure, and sediment management.
records.eligibility: The proposed project must appear on DEQ’s current eligible Agricultural BMP list.
records.requirements:
Be used to construct, renovate, improve, or equip a facility or structure that implements a DEQ-eligible agricultural BMP.
Have a clear purpose of preventing or reducing pollution of state waters.
Address agricultural pollutants such as sediment, nutrients, manure, animal waste, fertiliser, pesticides, contaminated stormwater, or erosion.
Produce a recognisable water-quality benefit. Projects with no recognisable water-quality benefit receive a low ranking and are denied funding.
Be operated and maintained for the life of the loan.
Continue to be used for its approved purpose as an agricultural BMP.
records.costShare: 0% interest; loan terms up to 10 years; potential principal forgiveness. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and evaluated monthly.
records.benefit: Low-cost financing for approved agricultural BMP construction and installation.
records.contacts: Phil Davis: 540-209-4201. Megan O'Gorek: 540-217-7155. DEQ Agricultural BMP Programs: 804-914-3729. DEQ main line: 804-698-4000.

records.name: Reforestation of Timberlands Program
records.problem: Cutover timberland; worn-out or underproductive fields; loss of tree cover; erosion; low forest productivity; need to transition marginal land to forest.
records.eligibility: Private Virginia landowners with land suitable for pine reforestation.
records.practice:
Cutover forestland, understocked land, or other suitable land where pine establishment is appropriate.
Eligible practices can include site preparation, planting or direct seeding, and other approved measures needed to establish pine.
.
records.costShare: Reimburses a portion of eligible pine-reforestation costs. Exact practice rates are provided in the current DOF program topic sheet and depend on available funding.
records.benefit: Cost-share reimbursement and professional forestry assistance.

records.name: Hardwood Initiative Cost-Share Program
records.problem: Degraded hardwood stands; invasive plants; poor regeneration; excessive competing vegetation; declining tree vigor; wildfire and climate stress.
records.eligibility:
Private landowners and other private ownership entities with eligible hardwood forestland.
Eligible ownership may include individuals, companies, limited liability companies, and nongovernmental organizations.
The property must contain at least five acres of forestland.
Cost share is generally available for a minimum treatment area of five acres and a maximum of 100 acres per tract per year.
A landowner may receive assistance on no more than 100 acres per year.
Invasive-plant control may be conducted on as little as one acre, provided the overall tract contains at least five acres of forest.
records.practice:
Potential Practices: Crop-tree release.
Precommercial thinning.
Midstory management.
Cull-tree control.
Timber-stand improvement.
Prescribed burning and burn preparation.
Invasive-plant control.
Stand marking.
records.costShare: 90% of actual cost, subject to practice-specific maximum rates. Examples published by DOF include up to $171/acre for crop-tree release, $225/acre for several stand-improvement practices, $270/acre for invasive control, and $36/acre for prescribed burning.
records.benefit: Reimbursement for approved hardwood-management work.

records.name: Growing and Protecting Forests Cost-Share Program
records.problem: Poor forest health; invasive plants; overstocked or underperforming pine and mixed stands; reduced resilience to drought, pests, storms, and wildfire.
records.eligibility:
Private forest landowners with eligible Virginia forestland.
The tract must generally contain at least five acres of forest.
Assistance is generally limited to 100 acres per tract per year and 100 acres per landowner per year.
records.costShare: 70% of total project cost, not to exceed the applicable practice-specific per-acre rate.
records.benefit: Partial reimbursement and forestry technical assistance.

records.name: Diminished Species Establishment Cost-Share Program
records.problem: Loss of native tree diversity; reduced forest resilience; degraded or simplified stands.
records.eligibility:
Virginia landowners with a site determined by DOF to be suitable for one or more eligible diminished tree species.
The applicant must work with a DOF forester before purchasing seedlings or beginning establishment work.
records.requirements:
Speices: American chestnut or approved chestnut planting material.
Red spruce.
Shortleaf pine
records.costShare: 90% of total project cost, not to exceed the current practice-specific per-acre rate.
records.benefit: Partial reimbursement for approved establishment expenses.

records.name: Riparian Forests for Landowners Program
records.problem: Streambank erosion; nutrient and sediment runoff; loss of shade and habitat; flooding; degraded field or forest edges near water.
records.eligibility: Private landowners with land suitable for establishment or restoration of a riparian forest buffer.
records.requirements:
The proposed planting must be associated with a stream, river, drainage feature, water body, or other qualifying riparian area.
The site must be capable of supporting an approved forest buffer. Projects may include site preparation, trees and shrubs, planting, seedling protection, and an initial maintenance period.
records.benefit: Design, planting, materials, installation, and limited maintenance assistance.

records.name: Logger Best Management Practice Cost-Share Program
records.problem: Sediment and erosion from logging roads and stream crossings; water-quality damage following timber harvests and intense rainfall.
records.eligibility:
Maintain current training through Virginia’s SHARP Logger Program.
Do not owe any outstanding debt to the Virginia Department of Forestry.
Do not have unresolved enforcement or corrective actions under Virginia’s Silvicultural Water Quality Law.
Have a timber-harvest stream crossing or related area that may deliver sediment into a stream.
Allow Virginia Department of Forestry water-quality staff to inspect the proposed crossing and develop an approved installation and closeout plan.
Receive program approval before beginning the funded work.
records.costShare: 75% of actual cost up to $6,000; maximum increases to $12,000 when the project includes purchase of a portable bridge.
records.benefit: Reimbursement for proper installation and closeout of timber-harvest stream crossings.

records.name: Virginia Clean Water Revolving Loan Fund — Living Shorelines
records.problem: Shoreline erosion; tidal flooding; marsh and habitat loss; wave damage; increasing exposure to saltwater on waterfront farms or forests.
records.eligibility: Direct applicants must be Virginia local governments. Loan funds must be used either for a locality’s own living-shoreline project or for an approved local program providing low-interest loans or incentives to individual citizens and certain qualifying coastal businesses. Every funded project must establish a qualifying living shoreline for the purpose of protecting or improving water quality and preventing pollution of state waters.
records.requirements:
The project must establish a qualifying living shoreline and must be designed to:

Protect or improve water quality.
Prevent pollution of Virginia state waters.
Address shoreline erosion using living or nature-based shoreline features rather than relying solely on conventional shoreline hardening
records.benefit: Financing for living-shoreline construction, either by a locality or through a local property-owner loan program.

records.name: Virginia Farmland Preservation Fund / Local Purchase of Development Rights Programs
records.problem: Development pressure; fragmentation; loss of working farms and forests; reduced ability to manage land for long-term climate resilience.
records.county: Only counties and cities with active local PDR programs
records.eligibility: Individual landowners generally apply through a participating county or city PDR program rather than directly to the state. The applicant must own qualifying Virginia farm or forest land, voluntarily agree to convey permanent development restrictions, demonstrate acceptable title, meet the locality’s parcel-ranking criteria, permit appraisal and due diligence, and execute a recorded agricultural conservation easement. State matching funds are awarded to qualifying local PDR programs and must be used to purchase development rights or conservation easements and to pay authorised transaction costs such as appraisals, surveys, title work, baseline documentation, closing, and recordation. The easement must permanently restrict incompatible development and subdivision, protect working farm or forest land, run with the land, bind future owners, and remain subject to monitoring and enforcement.
records.contacts: Office of Working Lands Preservation: 434-220-9021; conservation@dof.virginia.gov. .

records.name: Virginia Land Conservation Foundation Grants
records.problem: Loss of farmland, forest, wetlands, riparian corridors, floodplains, habitat, and open space with water-quality or climate-resilience value.
records.eligibility: Eligible applicants generally include Virginia state agencies, local governments, public bodies, recognised Virginia tribes, qualifying nonprofit land trusts, and other approved conservation entities. Private landowners generally participate through one of these eligible applicants. The project must acquire fee-simple ownership, a conservation or open-space easement, development rights, or another qualifying real-property interest and permanently protect significant farmland, forestland, habitat, ecological, historic, cultural, recreational, tribal, or open-space resources. Funds must be used for the approved acquisition and authorised transaction costs, such as the purchase price, appraisal, survey, title work, environmental review, baseline documentation, legal services, closing, and recordation. The property interest must be protected perpetually, the purchase price must be supported by an acceptable appraisal, required match must be documented, and the recipient must monitor and enforce the protected property after closing.
records.costShare: Competitive grant. Award amounts and matching requirements depend on the current grant round and project category.
records.contacts: DCR main office: 804-786-6124. Land-conservation program page and current grant contacts: https://www.dcr.virginia.gov/land-conservation/

records.name: Virginia Nonpoint-Source Nutrient Credit Certification Program
records.problem: Conversion of vulnerable or degraded land; nutrient runoff; stream or shoreline degradation; need for revenue to support permanent restoration.
records.county: Eligible watersheds and nutrient-credit service areas
records.eligibility: Eligible projects include approved practices that produce quantifiable nitrogen or phosphorus reductions beyond the applicable regulatory baseline
records.costShare: No fixed cost share. Certified nitrogen or phosphorus credits may be sold at market prices to eligible buyers; income is not guaranteed.

records.name: Virginia Department of Forestry Landowner Assistance and Forest Stewardship Planning
records.problem: Need for professional diagnosis and management planning for degraded forests, invasive species, storm damage, wildfire risk, declining tree health, or conversion of marginal agricultural land.
records.eligibility: Assistance is generally available to Virginia private forest landowners and owners of land suitable for forest establishment who are willing to identify management goals and permit a property assessment
records.practice: The plan may address reforestation, timber, wildlife, water quality, invasive species, forest health, recreation, wildfire risk, roads, stream crossings, and long-term conservation.
records.contacts: DOF main office: 434-977-6555. Find the local forester: https://dof.virginia.gov/about-us/contact-us/find-a-local-forester/

records.name: Virginia Forest Legacy Program
records.problem: Loss, conversion, and fragmentation of working forestland; degraded water quality; degraded wildlife habitat; loss of sensitive natural sites
records.agency: Virginia Department of Forestry (DOF); USDA Forest Service
records.eligibility: The project area must be located wholly or partially within the designated Forest Legacy Area. Each tract must be at least 100 acres and at least 75% forested. The title must be clear of liens/encumbrances, and existing mortgage holders must be willing to subordinate for an easement.
records.requirements: The landowner must be a willing seller; be willing to place a perpetual conservation easement on the property or sell it in fee simple; allow annual on-site monitoring if an easement is used; contribute toward due-diligence costs, usually at least 25%; provide or prepare a DOF-approved Forest Stewardship Management Plan; work with a Project Advocate; and sign a non-binding letter of intent before federal submission

records.name: Albemarle County Acquisition of Conservation Easements (ACE) Program
records.problem: Development pressure; subdivision and permanent conversion of family farms, forests, open space, and natural-resource land.
records.agency: Albemarle County Community Development; Albemarle Conservation Easement Authority
records.eligibility: Eligible property must be in Albemarle County and qualify under the County's ACE ordinance and ranking process. The County states that the program was designed especially to help landowners of modest means protect family farms.
records.requirements: The owner conveys a permanent conservation easement restricting future development.
records.practice: Purchase and record a permanent conservation easement.
records.strategies: The County states that payment may be up to 100% of the easement value using a sliding adjusted-gross-income scale.
records.benefit: Potential payment for the appraised conservation-easement value; permanent protection of the property. Current funding or application availability was not confirmed.

records.name: Loudoun County Conservation Easement Assistance Program
records.problem: High transaction costs that discourage owners from permanently preserving farms, forests, streams, scenic land, and open space.
records.eligibility: A Loudoun County landowner must work with a qualified land trust. The land trust applies on the landowner's behalf.
records.requirements: The property must be placed under a qualifying permanent conservation easement held by a land trust. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and funds are first-come, first-served, subject to available annual funding.
records.practice: Complete the legal, appraisal, survey, documentation, and stewardship work needed to establish a conservation easement.
records.strategies: Qualified expenses include attorney fees, land appraisal and survey fees, processing and document fees, and stewardship costs.
records.costShare: Reimbursement of qualifying easement expenses up to $25,000.
records.benefit: Reduces the upfront cost of permanently protecting a farm, forest, or other conservation land. County materials state that $150,000 is available annually, distributed first-come, first-served.

records.name: Fauquier County Purchase of Development Rights Program
records.problem: Development pressure, fragmentation, and loss of working farmland and rural natural resources.
records.eligibility: Farm owners with property that meets Fauquier County's PDR eligibility and development-right calculations may voluntarily apply. Final eligibility and number of eligible rights are determined by the County.
records.requirements: The owner sells eligible development rights to the County and records a permanent conservation easement. The owner retains the land and may continue agricultural and other easement-permitted uses.
records.practice: Sell development rights and permanently preserve the farm through a conservation easement.
records.strategies: The County website states that eligible development rights may be purchased for $60,000 per right. The number of rights and selection depend on County review and available funding.
records.benefit: $60,000 per eligible development right, subject to eligibility, selection, and available funding.

records.name: Clarke County Conservation Easement Authority Program
records.problem: Loss of agricultural, natural, scenic, historic, and forest resources through subdivision or development.
records.eligibility: Land must be in Clarke County and contain agricultural, natural, scenic, historic, or other conservation resources considered significant by the Authority.
records.requirements: A willing landowner works with the Authority to establish a permanent conservation easement. Easement terms and any purchase or donation arrangement are property-specific.
records.practice: Permanently restrict development through a conservation easement.
records.benefit: Permanent protection of qualifying agricultural, forest, scenic, natural, or historic land.

records.name: Stafford County Purchase of Development Rights Program
records.problem: Development pressure, fragmentation, and loss of rural land, farms, forests, water resources, and environmentally sensitive areas.
records.eligibility: The property must be in Stafford County and generally contain at least 20 acres, either as one parcel or contiguous parcels combined.
records.requirements: The owner records a permanent conservation easement restricting development. Farming, timbering, residence, and other uses allowed by the easement may continue. Applications are ranked and purchases are subject to available funding and County approval.
records.practice: Sell development rights and record a permanent conservation easement.
records.benefit: Payment based on the appraised conservation-easement value; permanent land protection.

records.name: Prince William County Purchase of Development Rights Program
records.problem: Development pressure and conversion of agricultural, forest, reservoir-protection, historic, park, and open-space land.
records.agency: Prince William County Environmental Management Office
records.eligibility: Eligible land generally must contain at least 20 acres, alone or as contiguous parcels; be located in an eligible Comprehensive Plan designation such as Agriculture and Forestry, Parks and Open Space, Occoquan Reservoir Protection Area, or County Registered Historic Site; and be capable of subdivision under County ordinance without Board approval.
records.requirements: The owner voluntarily conveys a permanent open-space easement restricting residential development. Agricultural, forestry, and other permitted uses may continue. Applications are reviewed, ranked, and selected by the Board subject to available funding.
records.practice: Sell residential development rights and permanently preserve the property.
records.strategies: The 2026 application period is July 1 through August 31, 2026.

records.name: Virginia Beach Agricultural Reserve Program
records.problem: Loss of productive farmland and agricultural economy through residential development and fragmentation.
records.agency: City of Virginia Beach Agriculture Department
records.eligibility: Property must meet the Agricultural Reserve Program's location, agricultural-use, acreage, and development-right eligibility requirements. The owner may offer development rights on all or part of an eligible property.
records.requirements: The owner voluntarily sells development rights and records a permanent agricultural conservation easement. The property remains privately owned and agricultural uses may continue under the easement.
records.practice: Sell development rights and retain land in permanent agricultural use.
records.strategies: The City evaluates eligible development rights and structures payment under the program agreement. The public program page reports 11,358 acres enrolled and 992 development rights captured.
records.benefit: Payment for retired development rights while the land remains privately owned and available for agriculture.
records.personnel:
Sarah Grimstead Cotten
Agricultural Reserve Program Coordinator

records.name: Chesapeake Open Space and Agriculture Preservation Program
records.problem: Conversion and fragmentation of farms, forests, open space, watersheds, wildlife habitat, and rural land.
records.eligibility: A willing landowner must own qualifying agricultural or open-space land in Chesapeake. Applications are evaluated for eligibility and, when applications compete for available funding, ranked under separate agricultural-land and open-space criteria.
records.requirements: The City purchases development rights in exchange for a permanent preservation easement. The owner retains ownership, may retain a home, and may continue agricultural or open-space uses permitted by the easement.
records.practice: Sell development rights and permanently preserve agricultural or open-space land.
records.strategies: The program pays fair market value for the development rights, subject to appraisal, ranking, approval, and available funding.
records.benefit: Fair-market-value payment for purchased development rights; continued private ownership and qualifying agricultural or open-space use.

records.name: NALF Fentress Encroachment Protection Acquisition Program
records.problem: Development encroachment near Naval Auxiliary Landing Field Fentress and loss of the area's rural and agricultural landscape.
records.agency: City of Chesapeake; U.S. Navy and conservation funding partners
records.eligibility: Limited to willing sellers of properties within the NALF Fentress Overlay District. Property eligibility and priority are determined through the competitive acquisition process.
records.requirements: The City purchases qualifying property in fee simple at fair market value. Unlike a conservation-easement program, the landowner sells the property rather than retaining ownership.
records.practice: Sell qualifying land for permanent conservation and encroachment protection.
records.strategies: The program is intended to prevent incompatible development and preserve the rural and agricultural character around NALF Fentress.
records.benefit: Fair-market-value purchase of qualifying property from willing sellers.

records.name: Fairfax County Conservation Assistance Program
records.problem: Erosion, excessive runoff, degraded drainage areas, compacted soil, loss of native vegetation, and small-scale stream or stormwater problems.
records.agency: Northern Virginia Soil and Water Conservation District; Fairfax County
records.eligibility: Available to eligible private properties, common-interest communities, houses of worship, and other applicants in the Northern Virginia Soil and Water Conservation District service area. Agricultural operations should confirm whether the proposed site is eligible for CAP/VCAP or should instead use agricultural BMP cost-share.
records.requirements: Applicants must receive technical review and approval before installation, follow the approved design, obtain required permits, maintain the practice, and submit documentation for reimbursement.
records.practice: Install an approved conservation landscaping, rain garden, vegetated stormwater conveyance, permeable surface, or other eligible stormwater practice.
records.strategies: County-funded CAP and state-funded VCAP reimburse approved stormwater practices. Published County meeting records show many conservation-landscaping reimbursements capped at $7,000, but rates and caps vary by practice and current policy.
records.costShare: Practice-specific reimbursement; examples in County records include up to $7,000 for conservation landscaping and larger amounts for some permeable-surface practices.
records.benefit: Cost-share reimbursement and technical assistance for approved land and stormwater improvements.

records.name: NFWF — National Coastal Resilience Fund
records.problem: Invests in nature-based solutions that reduce coastal hazard risk for communities while improving habitat for fish and wildlife.
records.eligibility: Projects must generally show dual benefits: coastal community risk reduction and habitat improvement. Private land projects may require landowner/manager support letters if applicant does not own/manage the land.
records.notes: Strong for living shorelines, marsh restoration, floodplain reconnection, wetland buffers, dunes, and other nature-based coastal protection near farms. Usually requires a partner applicant; farmer can be a site/landowner partner.

records.name: Chesapeake Bay Land and Water Initiative
records.problem: Loss of farmland and forestland, nutrient and sediment pollution, degraded riparian areas, wetland loss, and insufficient long-term stewardship
records.agency: Land Trust Alliance and participating land trusts
records.eligibility: Funding and technical support are generally accessed by land trusts and conservation organizations. Private landowners participate through an eligible land trust, conservation easement, stewardship project, or partner-led land-protection effort.
records.requirements: The property or project must provide meaningful conservation and water-quality benefits and comply with the participating land trust's due diligence, easement, stewardship, monitoring, or acquisition requirements.
records.practice: Conservation easement
records.strategies: Potential support may include permanent land protection, riparian or wetland stewardship, conservation planning, and land-trust capacity needed to complete projects in the Chesapeake Bay watershed.
records.notes: Not a direct application program for most farmers. Contact a local accredited land trust and ask whether the property could fit a Chesapeake Bay land-protection or stewardship project supported through this initiative.

records.name: Chesapeake Bay Trust – Outreach and Restoration Grant
records.agency: Chesapeake Bay Trust and Charles County
records.eligibility: Typically nonprofits, local governments, schools, community associations, faith-based groups, and other organizations. Farmers usually need a partner organization.
records.requirements: Farmers should team with a nonprofit, county, watershed group, or soil conservation district and use the farm as the demonstration/restoration site.
records.strategies: Up to $125,000 depending on project type.

records.name: Community Impact Grants
records.problem: Community environmental needs, conservation access, food-system resilience, and limited nonprofit capacity to assist farms and natural lands
records.eligibility: Delaware nonprofit organizations meeting the active grant-cycle requirements. Individual farmers and forest owners generally need a nonprofit applicant or fiscal sponsor.
records.requirements: Applicants must address an eligible community need, submit the required proposal and budget, and comply with grant-management and reporting requirements.
records.practice: Partner-led conservation or community agriculture project
records.strategies: Funding priorities vary. Conservation, agriculture, food access, community resilience, and environmental projects may qualify when they match the current grant opportunity.
records.notes: Not a direct farmer grant. Farmers should partner with a Delaware conservation nonprofit, food-system organization, land trust, or community group and confirm the active funding priorities.

records.name: Inland Bays Land Conservation and Easement Assistance
records.scopeDetail: Delaware — Sussex County and Inland Bays watershed
records.problem: Development pressure, loss of forests and wetlands, habitat fragmentation, shoreline and water-quality degradation
records.agency: Delaware Center for the Inland Bays and conservation partners
records.eligibility: Private owners of farms, forests, wetlands, or other conservation-priority land in the Inland Bays watershed. Property eligibility depends on conservation value and partner priorities.
records.requirements: Landowners entering an easement must accept permanent development restrictions and allow monitoring in accordance with the easement agreement.
records.practice: Conservation easement
records.strategies: Potential benefits may include land-protection assistance, partner-supported restoration, tax benefits, or payment when acquisition funding is available. Payment is not guaranteed.
records.notes: An easement donation is not the same as a grant. Farmers should ask whether the transaction is donated, bargain-sale, or purchased, and obtain independent legal and tax advice.

records.name: Young, Beginning, and Small Farmer Grant Program
records.scopeDetail: Delaware and other Horizon Farm Credit service areas
records.problem: Limited farm start-up or expansion capital, inadequate equipment, water-management needs, and barriers faced by young, beginning, or small farmers
records.eligibility: Applicants must reside in Horizon Farm Credit's eligible territory and meet at least one program category, such as being age 18–35, having ten years or less of Schedule F farm income, or operating a farm with less than the program's gross cash-income threshold.
records.requirements: Applicants must submit the required business and project information and use any award for approved on-farm needs in accordance with the grant agreement.
records.practice: Farm equipment or infrastructure purchase
records.strategies: Recent program materials announced competitive grants of $20,000. Potential uses may include irrigation, grazing infrastructure, water systems, soil-health equipment, drainage adaptation, or resilient farm infrastructure when allowed.
records.notes: Applicants do not necessarily need to be Horizon Farm Credit borrowers. Confirm territorial eligibility, current deadline, number of awards, and allowable expenses.

records.name: Open Space Institute — Delaware River Watershed Protection Fund
records.problem: Provides grants and low-cost loans for land protection and conservation planning in the Delaware River watershed, often through land trusts and conservation partners.
records.eligibility: Usually for land trusts, nonprofits, and conservation partners rather than individual farmers. Farmers may participate through land/easement sale or partner-led project.
records.contacts: Bill Rawlyk, brawlyk@osiny.org, 908-642-4747. Catalyst Grants: Hallie Schwab, hschwab@osiny.org, 929-405-3294.
records.notes: Strong option for preserving forests, wetlands, riparian areas, and high-priority watershed lands. Farmers should approach a land trust or OSI contact if property has water-quality, forest, or conservation value.

records.name: William Penn Foundation — Watershed Protection Grants
records.problem: Large regional philanthropy supporting Delaware River watershed protection, restoration, land protection, water quality, and resilience through nonprofit partners.
records.eligibility: Generally nonprofit and partner-led; farmers are more likely to benefit as project participants or landowner partners than as direct applicants.
records.contacts: General website: https://williampennfoundation.org/. Media contact listed publicly: Rebecca Morley, rmorley@williampennfoundation.org, 215-988-1830.
records.notes: Not a direct farmer grant. Important because it funds many Delaware River watershed partners. Farmers should connect through nonprofits, watershed groups, land trusts, or NJ Audubon/NFWF/OSI-type partners.

records.name: NFWF — Delaware Watershed Conservation Fund
records.scopeDetail: Delaware River Watershed: NJ, DE, PA, NY
records.problem: Funds partner-led projects in the Delaware River watershed that reduce flooding and runoff, restore fish and wildlife habitat, improve water quality, and enhance public access.
records.eligibility: Eligible applicants generally include nonprofit 501(c) organizations, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal governments/organizations, and educational institutions. Individuals/private farmers usually need a partner applicant.
records.contacts: Erin Lewis, Program Director: erin.lewis@nfwf.org, (202) 595-2413; Evie Kraner: evie.kraner@nfwf.org, (202) 595-2651; Ragan Smith: ragan.smith@nfwf.org, (202) 938-0625.
records.notes: Excellent fit for Cumberland/Cape May/Delaware Bay projects if framed as flooding/runoff reduction, water quality, wetland restoration, habitat, buffers, or marsh migration. Farmers should partner with a land trust, conservation district, nonprofit, municipality, or university.

records.name: Chesapeake Bay Trust – Grants & Opportunities
records.problem: Water-quality degradation, habitat loss, restoration needs

records.name: Healthy Forests, Healthy Waters
records.problem: Nutrient and sediment runoff, poor water quality, limited forest cover, degraded habitat, and reduced land resilience
records.agency: Alliance for the Chesapeake Bay; Maryland Forest Service; Maryland Forestry Foundation
records.eligibility: Privately owned open land of one acre or more; plantings as small as 0.5 acre may be considered. Existing woodlands are not eligible for understory planting. Land cannot already be required to be reforested under regulation
records.requirements: Landowners must keep the trees for at least 10 years, assume responsibility for maintenance after the third growing season, and maintain the installed practice according to the approved project plan. No restrictive conservation easement is required
records.practice: Riparian buffer planting; tree planting; road stabilization / erosion control / sediment reduction.

records.name: Maryland Grazers Network
records.problem: Pasture degradation, stream impacts, limited grazing expertise, weak farm profitability, and inadequate grazing infrastructure
records.eligibility: Maryland livestock, dairy, sheep, poultry, or other grazing producers seeking to establish or improve managed grazing systems.
records.requirements: Participants work with mentors or technical specialists and implement an appropriate grazing-management approach. Additional funding may have separate eligibility rules.
records.practice: Managed grazing mentorship and implementation
records.strategies: Support may include producer mentorship, grazing expertise, financial management, marketing assistance, pasture planning, fencing, livestock water, and connections to funding.
records.notes: Primarily technical and financial-access assistance rather than a guaranteed cash grant. Ask which expenses, planning services, or implementation practices are presently funded.

records.name: Keep Maryland Beautiful
records.agency: The Chesapeake Bay Trust and Maryland Environmental Trust (MET), Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA), and the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT).

records.name: Aileen Hughes Award Program
records.agency:
The Chesapeake Bay Trust (Trust) and the Maryland
Environmental Trust (MET)
records.eligibility: awarded annually to an individual representing a Maryland land trust who has demonstrated outstanding leadership in land conservation.
records.requirements: Maryland land trusts can nominate an individual from their own land trust or another Maryland land trust
records.strategies: Up to $5,000

records.name: Eastern Shore Land Conservancy
records.scopeDetail: Maryland — Eastern Shore: Maryland Eastern Shore: Cecil, Kent, Queen Anne’s, Caroline, Talbot, Dorchester
records.eligibility: Protects and stewards farmland, wetlands, forests, and rural landscapes on Maryland’s Eastern Shore using easements, stewardship, advocacy, transfers, and acquisitions.
records.requirements: Landowners on Maryland’s Eastern Shore with farmland, wetlands, forests, or conservation-priority properties.
records.contacts: 114 S. Washington St., Suite 101, Easton, MD 21601; info@eslc.org.     form: https://www.eslc.org/how-can-we-help-you-conserve/
records.notes: Useful for landowners interested not only in land protection/easements, but also restoration practices that improve water quality, biodiversity, coastal resilience, and habitat

records.name: Farm and Watershed Restoration Partnerships
records.problem: Streambank erosion, inadequate riparian cover, pasture impacts, nutrient runoff, and watershed degradation
records.eligibility: Private farmers and landowners in eligible CBF project areas with a suitable restoration, grazing, tree, stream, or water-quality project.
records.requirements: Participants work with CBF and its partners on planning, funding, installation, maintenance, and any monitoring or reporting requirements.
records.practice: Riparian restoration
records.strategies: CBF programs may support grazing, stream restoration, tree planting, buffers, and other watershed practices through charitable and public-private funding.
records.notes: Broad umbrella entry. In a final master spreadsheet, the Maryland Grazers Network and Mountains-to-Bay Grazing Alliance may be more useful as separate, specific programs.

records.name: ShoreRivers — Agriculture / Restoration
records.problem: Nutrient runoff, sediment loss, water quality degradation
records.requirements: Farmer/landowner submits a project inquiry form; ShoreRivers evaluates, designs, funds, and manages eligible restoration or research projects
records.strategies: Designs, funds, and manages agricultural restoration projects that reduce sediment and nutrient pollution. Provides engineering, geospatial, and technical assistance to support project planning and implementation

records.name: Agricultural Restoration Assistance
records.problem: Nutrient and sediment runoff, wetland loss, riparian degradation, drainage problems, habitat loss, and farm water-quality impacts
records.eligibility: Farmers and agricultural landowners in ShoreRivers service watersheds with suitable conservation or restoration projects.
records.requirements: Landowner works with ShoreRivers and project partners on site assessment, design, permitting, funding, implementation, and required maintenance.
records.practice: Agricultural best-management-practice installation
records.strategies: Projects may include wetlands, tree planting, drainage improvements, stream restoration, buffers, nutrient reduction, and other agricultural conservation practices.
records.notes: ShoreRivers may combine nonprofit grants with government cost share. Farmers should ask what share of design, permitting, installation, and maintenance expenses will remain their responsibility.

records.name: Agricultural Conservation Drainage Projects
records.problem: Excess water, poor drainage, nutrient loss through drainage systems, low field trafficability, and altered agricultural hydrology
records.eligibility: Agricultural properties in eligible Eastern Shore watersheds with suitable drainage and water-quality conditions. Project participation depends on site assessment and available funding.
records.requirements: Landowner must cooperate with engineering, monitoring, installation, maintenance, and data-collection requirements established for the project.
records.practice: Controlled drainage
records.strategies: Projects may involve controlled drainage, treatment wetlands, improved tile-drainage management, and related water-control systems intended to maintain production while reducing nutrient losses.
records.notes: Conservation drainage does not directly reverse salinity. Farms affected by saltwater intrusion need hydrologic and soil assessment before drainage changes are recommended.

records.name: Lower Shore Land Trust — Conservation Easements (LSLT)
records.scopeDetail: Maryland Lower Eastern Shore (Worcester, Wicomico, and Somerset counties)
records.problem: Soil health; water quality; wildlife habitat; forest lands
records.eligibility: Agricultural lands, wetlands, and forest lands
records.requirements: Written agreement between a landowner and a land trust or government agency; property remains in private ownership; development is limited according to the easement
records.practice: Conservation easement
records.notes: LSLT helps landowners identify conservation and restoration goals and match their property with appropriate conservation programs and cost-share opportunities. Easements may provide considerable federal and state tax benefits, according to the brochure.

records.name: Scenic Rivers Land Trust — Conservation Easements
records.problem: Degraded water quality; stormwater runoff; pollutant runoff; wetland degradation; degraded wildlife habitat; loss of forest and farmland
records.eligibility: Scenic Rivers considers properties with conservation values such as: generally 10 acres or more of undeveloped land; high-functioning forests, wetlands, meadows, ecosystems, or natural features; endangered, threatened, or priority species; scenic open space providing public benefit; connections to other protected open space or wildlife corridors; or land in agricultural use
records.requirements: Each easement must be approved by the Scenic Rivers Board of Directors. The property and proposed easement are evaluated for development rights eliminated, reserved residences or subdivisions, continuity of open land, monitoring and enforcement feasibility, property size, conservation value, consistency with land-use policies, management potential, legal access for monitoring, hazards, and existing easements or restrictions

records.name: American Farmland Trust — Brighter Future Fund / National Farm Viability Grant
records.problem: Provides direct grants to farmers and ranchers to improve farm viability, resilience, land access, stewardship, and long-term operation stability.
records.eligibility: For-profit U.S. farmers or ranchers engaged in terrestrial, soil-based agricultural production; operation must have produced more than $1,000 in agricultural products sold, bartered, or exchanged in the most recent growing year.
records.notes: Strong direct-to-farmer option. Frame saltwater intrusion as farm viability, climate resilience, soil health, infrastructure, regenerative transition, or land stewardship.

records.name: Preservation Trust Fund
records.agency: the Virginia Outdoors Foundation (VOF), the Open-Space Lands Preservation Trust Fund (PTF
records.eligibility:
kh Preservation Trust Fund grant may be awarded to:

An individual.
A private landowner.
An organisation.
A nonprofit entity.
A local government.
Another applicant with a qualifying real-estate interest to convey.Must not generally already be protected through an existing open-space easement or similar deed restriction.
Must be permanently dedicated as open-space land.
Must be consistent with the locality’s official comprehensive plan.
Must convey an enforceable real-estate interest to VOF or a locality.
Must protect the conservation values for which the grant was awarded.
Should not be predominantly covered by buildings, pavement, or other hardscape.
May have to undergo parcel consolidation if the number of existing tax parcels exceeds what the final protection instrument permits.
records.strategies: Income-based assistance may cover up to 100% or $20,000 for income up to $95,000; 75% or $15,000 for $96,000–$110,000; 50% or $10,000 for $111,000–$125,000; and up to 50% of survey cost or $10,000 for $125,000–$200,000, subject to current rules and funding.
records.contacts: Email: grants@vof.org. VOF main office: 540-347-7727. https://www.vof.org/contact/

records.name: The FruitGuys Community Fund — Small Farm Grants
records.problem: Supports small farms and agricultural nonprofits with sustainability projects that benefit the environment, local food systems, and farm diversity.
records.eligibility: Small U.S. farms of 250 acres or less; applicant must be farm owner/operator or have long-term legal land access. For-profit farms must be active for at least 2 years. Agricultural nonprofits must be 501(c)(3) and operating for at least 3 years.
records.notes: Good for smaller adaptation projects: soil health, native plantings, drainage-related resilience, sustainable infrastructure, pollinator/habitat work, or crop transition. 2026 cycle noted as closed on program page, so farmers should monitor next round.

records.name: Farm Aid — Farmer Hotline / Family Farm Disaster Fund
records.problem: Connects farmers to assistance and may provide emergency/disaster grants to individual farm families in hardship, especially through Farm Aid’s hotline process.
records.eligibility: Farmers needing assistance; Farm Aid evaluates farmer needs through its hotline and assistance process.
records.notes: Best for acute hardship or disaster-related financial stress, not for planned conservation projects. Farmers should clearly explain how flooding/salinity is affecting household, farm viability, or disaster recovery.

records.name: Ducks Unlimited — Conservation Easement Program
records.problem: Wetland loss, habitat degradation, development pressure, flood vulnerability, declining water quality.Ducks Unlimited, through their affiliate Wetlands America Trust, will put a permanent easement on your land and restore wetlands on your property. The easement document is tailored to meet the needs and interests of the landowner. DU will monitor the property on a yearly basis to make sure habitat is conserved. This could result in reduced income and estate taxes.
records.eligibility: The landowner will need to have owned the land for a certain amount of time in order to be eligible. Property must provide conservation value by protecting: (1) outdoor recreation or public education; (2) relatively natural habitat for fish, wildlife, or plants; (3) open space, including farmland or forestland, that provides scenic enjoyment, supports a federal, state, or local conservation policy, or preserves historically important land or certified historic structures.
records.requirements: Landowner voluntarily grants a conservation easement. DU evaluates the property, develops easement terms, completes appraisal/title work, records the easement, and conducts long-term monitoring.Ducks Unlimited will focus on properties that fall within their priority areas, but they do take easements outside their areas as well
records.practice: Conservation easement
