records.name: New Jersey Conservation Foundation — Land Conservation / Easements
records.problem: Works with landowners to preserve land through conservation easements, farmland easements, fee-simple acquisitions, reserved life estates, remainder interests, and bequests.
records.eligibility: Land must meet NJ Conservation Foundation project criteria and conservation priorities. Easements restrict development while land may remain privately owned; farmland easements limit future use to agriculture.
records.notes: Best for farms where land preservation, development-rights sale, wetland/forest protection, or long-term family ownership is more important than short-term operating support.

records.name: NJ SADC — Grants to Nonprofits for Farmland Preservation
records.problem: Provides grants to nonprofit organizations to preserve farmland through fee simple acquisition or development easement acquisition.
records.eligibility: Nonprofit applicants must apply; farm must meet farmland preservation eligibility requirements, including SADC criteria, farmland tax assessment, and location in an agricultural development area where applicable.
records.contacts: SADC main farmland preservation page: https://www.nj.gov/agriculture/sadc/farmpreserve/. Farmers should also contact their County Agriculture Development Board.
records.notes: Not private money, but important because nonprofits can use this pathway to pay farmers for preservation. Useful for landowners considering easement sale or farm preservation as an adaptation strategy.

records.name: Sustainable Agriculture Enterprise Land Access Program (SAgE)
records.scopeDetail: New Jersey — participating SAgE locations, especially northern New Jersey
records.problem: Lack of affordable farmland, insecure land tenure, barriers for beginning or underserved farmers, and difficulty investing in long-term soil stewardship
records.eligibility: Experienced farmers seeking land for an independent farm business and willing to follow the program's land-management and production expectations. Specific experience, business-plan, and production requirements apply.
records.requirements: Participants enter a lease, comply with property and conservation requirements, maintain required insurance and records, and operate according to approved organic or regenerative practices.
records.practice: Long-term affordable farmland lease
records.strategies: Provides affordable, longer-term access to preserved farmland. It is not an incubator and generally expects farmers to have sufficient experience and business capacity.
records.notes: Land access rather than a cash grant. Secure tenure may make conservation investment and long-term soil improvement financially feasible.

records.name: Leopold Conservation Award
records.scopeDetail: Participating U.S. states; availability varies by year
records.problem: Soil degradation, water-quality problems, habitat loss, and lack of recognition or flexible funding for exemplary private-land conservation
records.agency: Sand County Foundation and state-level partners
records.eligibility: Agricultural landowners in participating states who demonstrate outstanding voluntary conservation on working land. Nomination procedures and eligible landowner categories vary by state.
records.requirements: Applicant or nominee must complete the state award process and document conservation leadership, stewardship results, and operation-level practices.
records.practice: Whole-farm conservation stewardship
records.strategies: Competitive recognition award that generally includes a monetary prize. Award availability, amount, nomination deadlines, and eligible states vary.
records.notes: An award rather than project cost share. Confirm that the relevant state has an active program before recommending it to a landowner.

records.name: Sustainable Forestry and African American Land Retention Network
records.scopeDetail: Southern United States, including participating Virginia service areas
records.problem: Heirs-property risk, unclear title, loss of family forestland, limited forest income, and barriers to conservation-program participation
records.agency: Sustainable Forestry and African American Land Retention Network and regional anchor organizations
records.eligibility: Primarily serves African American family forest owners in participating Southern states and service regions. Eligibility and services depend on the local anchor organization and landownership circumstances.
records.requirements: Landowners work with network partners on forestry planning, legal or heirs-property issues, land retention, and implementation of sustainable forest-management recommendations.
records.practice: Forest-management planning
records.strategies: Assistance may include title and succession support, forestry advice, management plans, connections to timber and conservation markets, and help accessing public or private funding.
records.notes: Usually provides services and financial-access assistance rather than an unrestricted cash grant. Especially valuable when unresolved ownership or heirs-property issues prevent access to easements, carbon contracts, cost share, or disaster assistance.

records.name: Family Forest Carbon Program
records.problem: Forest degradation, reduced forest resilience, loss of wildlife habitat, and limited income for long-term sustainable forest management
records.agency: American Forest Foundation and The Nature Conservancy
records.eligibility: Generally privately owned family forestland with at least 30 forested acres in an eligible program area. The property and proposed practices must pass program screening.
records.requirements: Landowner enters a long-term agreement, generally 20 years, and implements approved forest-management practices. Harvesting and management restrictions vary by enrollment option.
records.practice: Improved forest management
records.strategies: Professional forestry consultation and a forest-management plan are included. Payments depend on property location, acreage, forest condition, and selected practices.
records.notes: Direct private carbon payment rather than a grant. Landowners should review harvest limits, payment timing, monitoring, reversal provisions, and compatibility with easements or other incentive programs before signing.

records.name: LandYield Forest Carbon Program
records.problem: Loss of forest carbon, pressure to harvest timber, forest degradation, and lack of recurring income for private woodland owners
records.agency: LandYield, in collaboration with Finite Carbon
records.requirements: United States — qualifying private forests
records.practice: Forest degradation, premature harvesting, limited access to forest-carbon markets, and insufficient income for long-term stewardship
records.strategies: CORE Carbon
records.notes: https://www.finitecarbon.com/

records.name: Soil and Water Outcomes Fund
records.problem: Nutrient loss, sediment runoff, greenhouse-gas emissions, declining soil health, and water-quality impairment
records.eligibility: Farmers must operate eligible cropland in an active project area and propose qualifying new or expanded conservation practices. Field history and prior practice adoption are reviewed.
records.requirements: Farmer implements contracted practices, supplies management information, permits measurement or modeling of environmental outcomes, and follows rules preventing duplicate sale of the same environmental outcome.
records.practice: Cover cropping
records.strategies: Payments are generally tied to quantified greenhouse-gas and water-quality outcomes. Eligible practices, crops, payment structure, and stacking rules vary by project and enrollment year.
records.notes: Direct annual ecosystem-service payment rather than a traditional reimbursement grant. Confirm whether the farm may combine the payment with federal or state cost share without double-counting environmental credits.

records.name: Farmer Veteran Fellowship Fund
records.problem: Limited farm start-up or expansion capital, inadequate conservation equipment, water-management needs, and barriers faced by military-veteran farmers
records.eligibility: Applicants generally must be U.S. military veterans or currently serving members who are beginning or expanding an agricultural operation. Detailed service, business, ownership, and application requirements vary by cycle.
records.requirements: Awardees use funds or donated equipment for approved farm-business needs and comply with application, vendor, documentation, and reporting requirements.
records.practice: Purchase of conservation equipment
records.strategies: Awards commonly support equipment or supplies rather than unrestricted cash. Conservation-related uses may be possible when they directly support the approved agricultural business plan.
records.notes: Not specifically a land-preservation program, but potentially useful for eligible veteran farmers purchasing equipment or infrastructure that improves grazing, water management, soil health, or farm resilience.

records.name: Fund-a-Farmer Grants
records.scopeDetail: United States — annual grant availability and eligible states may vary
records.problem: Pasture degradation, livestock water-management problems, inadequate fencing, animal-welfare concerns, and limited infrastructure for pasture-based production
records.eligibility: Generally intended for independent livestock or poultry farmers seeking to improve animal welfare and pasture-based systems. Specific species, farm-size, location, and operating-history requirements vary by grant cycle.
records.requirements: Funds must be used for an approved project and recipients must comply with the grant agreement, documentation, project completion, and reporting requirements.
records.practice: Pasture improvement
records.strategies: Past eligible expenses have included fencing, water systems, mobile housing, pasture improvements, and other infrastructure that supports humane, pasture-based livestock production.
records.notes: Small competitive grant and not relevant to most crop-only or forest operations. Verify that a current application cycle is open and that the applicant's species, location, and farm structure qualify.

records.name: Farmer-Led Research and Education Funding
records.scopeDetail: United States — current call and applicant eligibility must be confirmed
records.problem: Soil-health decline, climate stress, production uncertainty, and lack of on-farm research about resilient or organic practices
records.eligibility: Eligibility depends on the active funding opportunity. Projects generally must address organic or transitioning-organic production and may require a farmer-researcher, nonprofit, or academic partnership.
records.requirements: Projects must follow an approved research plan, collect and report data, share findings, and comply with the active request for proposals and organic-research requirements.
records.practice: On-farm research trial
records.strategies: Potential applications include trials of soil-health practices, salt-tolerant crops, amendments, crop rotations, drainage adaptations, or other climate-resilience strategies when allowed by the active solicitation.
records.notes: Research funding rather than ordinary conservation reimbursement. Do not list a deadline or award amount unless confirmed from a current request for proposals.

records.name: Reforestation Project Partnerships
records.scopeDetail: United States — projects selected through nonprofit and restoration partners
records.problem: Deforestation, degraded riparian areas, erosion, habitat loss, poor water quality, and marginal or repeatedly disturbed land
records.eligibility: Projects are generally proposed and managed by nonprofit, community, tribal, conservation, or restoration partners. Private landowners usually need an eligible project partner and a site suitable for ecologically appropriate tree establishment.
records.requirements: Project partners must submit an approved reforestation proposal, conduct planting and maintenance, document survival and outcomes, and comply with reporting and monitoring requirements.
records.practice: Tree planting
records.strategies: Potential projects include riparian buffers, restoration of degraded forestland, post-disturbance reforestation, habitat corridors, and conversion of marginal land to appropriate native woody vegetation.
records.notes: Partner-led funding rather than unrestricted money to an individual landowner. Farmers should approach a watershed group, land trust, conservation nonprofit, or restoration organization that could sponsor and manage the planting project.

records.name: Forest Carbon Works
records.scopeDetail: United States — property feasibility screening required
records.problem: Forest degradation, loss of standing carbon, pressure for near-term timber harvest, and limited access to forest-carbon revenue
records.eligibility: Private forestland with sufficient acreage, standing timber, carbon potential, and management flexibility to support project development, inventory, monitoring, and verification. Minimum viable acreage is property-specific.
records.requirements: Landowner enters a forest-carbon agreement, implements an approved management plan, maintains required carbon stocks, and permits inventory, monitoring, reporting, and verification.
records.practice: Avoided or deferred timber harvest
records.strategies: Project economics depend on acreage, forest type, current stocking, harvest history, baseline projections, carbon-credit price, and development costs.
records.notes: Not guaranteed funding. Compare proposals from multiple carbon developers and obtain independent legal and forestry review of credit ownership, fees, harvest limitations, permanence, reversal risk, and payment schedule.

records.name: CORE Carbon
records.problem: Forest degradation, premature harvesting, limited access to forest-carbon markets, and insufficient income for long-term stewardship
records.eligibility: Designed to aggregate smaller private and non-industrial forest properties, historically including properties in the approximate 40–5,000-acre range. Property feasibility and geographic availability must be confirmed.
records.requirements: Participating landowners implement an approved improved-forest-management project and comply with inventory, monitoring, reporting, verification, and carbon-credit requirements.
records.practice: Improved forest management
records.strategies: Projects may involve extending rotations, retaining additional standing timber, or other management changes that increase carbon storage relative to an approved baseline.
records.notes: Potential overlap with LandYield because LandYield works with Finite Carbon. Keep as a separate entry only when distinguishing the underlying carbon project platform from the landowner-facing enrollment service.

records.name: Sustainable Forestry Initiative Conservation Grants
records.problem: Forest biodiversity loss, degraded habitat, poor water quality, climate vulnerability, and unsustainable forest management
records.eligibility: Applicants are generally nonprofit organizations, academic institutions, Indigenous organizations, government entities, SFI-certified organizations, or other eligible partners. Individual private landowners generally participate through an applicant organization.
records.requirements: Projects must align with the active request for proposals and typically require defined conservation outcomes, work plans, budgets, reporting, and collaboration with relevant forest-sector or community partners.
records.practice: Forest habitat restoration
records.strategies: Funding priorities may include biodiversity, climate resilience, species conservation, water quality, conservation research, and responsible forest management. Priorities and deadlines vary by grant cycle.
records.notes: Partner-accessed funding, not normally a direct farmer or forest-owner grant. A private property may serve as a demonstration, restoration, monitoring, or research site within a nonprofit- or university-led project.

records.name: Producer-Led Agricultural Practices Program
records.scopeDetail: Upper Choptank watershed — Maryland and Delaware
records.problem: Nutrient runoff, drainage problems, water-quality degradation, insufficient conservation-practice adoption, and fragmented project delivery
records.agency: Envision the Choptank, ShoreRivers, and project partners
records.eligibility: Agricultural producers in the eligible Upper Choptank project area who are willing to participate in producer-led planning and conservation-practice development.
records.requirements: Participants collaborate with the producer group and project partners to identify, design, bundle, and implement qualifying agricultural conservation practices.
records.practice: Producer-led conservation practice planning
records.strategies: Potential practices may include drainage improvements, buffers, wetlands, nutrient-management improvements, and field-scale water-control projects, depending on the active initiative.
records.notes: Nonprofit-administered partnership with mixed funding. Farmers should confirm current enrollment geography, available practices, implementation funding, and whether participation requires a formal producer-group commitment.

records.name: Virginia Environmental Endowment — Community Conservation / Water Quality Grants
records.problem: Supports conservation, water quality restoration/improvement, land conservation, environmental literacy, and watershed protection in eligible areas.
records.eligibility: Nonprofits, tax-exempt organizations, local governments, soil and water conservation districts, agencies, tribes, and educational institutions. Not individuals or for-profit businesses.
records.strategies: Farmers should partner with a SWCD, nonprofit, watershed group, or local government. This is not a direct farmer grant.
records.contacts: Virginia Environmental Endowment: info@vee.org; P.O. Box 790, Richmond, VA 23218-0790. James River program: jrwqip@vee.org.

records.name: Virginia Eastern Shore Land Trust — Conservation Easements
records.problem: Protection and restoration of waters; preservation of farm and forestland; conservation of wildlife habitat; protection of natural, scenic, or historic features from excess future development
records.eligibility: Not specified
records.requirements: The landowner enters into a voluntary deeded conservation easement that permanently limits future development. The easement remains with the property when it is sold or transferred. Prospective donors are encouraged to involve family members, heirs, attorneys, and estate planners.
records.practice: Conservation easement

records.name: Regenerate Virginia Healthy Soils Grant
records.problem: Soil degradation, declining soil health, reduced biodiversity, climate vulnerability, and limited resources for regenerative practice adoption
records.agency: American Farmland Trust and Virginia Soil Health Coalition
records.eligibility: Virginia farmers and ranchers meeting the active grant-cycle requirements. Applicants must operate an eligible agricultural operation and propose a qualifying soil-health or regenerative-agriculture project.
records.requirements: Recipients must implement the approved project, document expenses and outcomes, and comply with the grant agreement and reporting requirements.
records.practice: Soil-health practice implementation
records.strategies: Recent rounds have supported practices such as diversified cover crops, biochar, rotational grazing, and other regenerative practices. Award limits and eligible expenses vary by cycle.
records.notes: Direct private grant to producers. Recent rounds have offered awards up to approximately $30,000, but current availability, deadline, award size, and eligible practices must be confirmed before application.

records.name: Regenerate Virginia Farm Vitality Grant
records.problem: Farm-business vulnerability, limited capital for adaptation, weak succession planning, and difficulty financing regenerative or diversified farm systems
records.eligibility: Virginia farmers and ranchers meeting the current grant-cycle requirements. Leaseholders may qualify when they can demonstrate sufficient tenure for the proposed investment.
records.requirements: Funds must be used for approved farm-viability purposes and recipients must complete required documentation, implementation, and reporting.
records.practice: Farm resilience equipment or planning
records.strategies: Potential uses include equipment, enterprise diversification, regenerative-system transition, succession planning, business planning, financial management, and professional services.
records.notes: Direct private grant to producers. Recent rounds have offered awards up to approximately $25,000. Confirm the current application cycle and allowable expenses.

records.name: Virginia Environmental Endowment — Virginia Program
records.problem: Water pollution, natural-resource degradation, land-conservation needs, and environmental restoration
records.eligibility: Eligible nonprofit organizations and qualifying project partners. Individual farmers and forest owners generally participate through a nonprofit-led project rather than applying directly.
records.requirements: Projects must align with the Endowment's active priorities and satisfy application, budget, grant-management, and reporting requirements.
records.practice: Partner-led land or water conservation project
records.notes: Partner-accessed private foundation funding. Farmers should approach a watershed group, land trust, university, or conservation nonprofit with a specific project site and documented environmental benefit.

records.name: Virginia Outdoors Foundation — Preservation Trust Fund
records.eligibility: PTF grants may pay for costs associated with the conveyance of an interest, right, or privilege in open space under the Open-Space Land Act including fee-simple acquisition, public access rights of way, due diligence, legal and survey costs.
records.practice: This is not operating money. It is best for landowners considering a conservation easement or permanent land-protection transaction. $1.8 million dollars for public access as well as natural and cultural resource protection projects.
records.notes: https://www.vof.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/FY27-Grant-Timeline.pdf

records.name: James River Water Quality Improvement Program
records.problem: Nutrient pollution, erosion, shoreline degradation, riparian loss, and impaired water quality
records.eligibility: Primarily nonprofit applicants and eligible project partners working in the James River watershed. Private landowners generally participate as host sites or landowner partners.
records.requirements: Projects must demonstrate measurable James River water-quality benefits and comply with the current program's application, implementation, and reporting requirements.
records.practice: Riparian or shoreline restoration
records.strategies: Projects  include living shorelines, riparian restoration, erosion control, nutrient reduction, and related watershed improvements.
records.notes: Best suited to landowners working with a James River watershed nonprofit or conservation organization. Confirm that a current funding round is active before listing a deadline.

records.name: Mountains-to-Bay Grazing Alliance
records.scopeDetail: Virginia and Maryland; Chesapeake Bay region
records.problem: Pasture degradation, streambank damage, livestock exclusion needs, inadequate fencing and water systems, and reduced grazing resilience
records.agency: Chesapeake Bay Foundation and partner organizations
records.eligibility: Livestock producers in participating service areas who are interested in adopting or improving managed grazing systems.
records.requirements: Participants work with grazing specialists, develop an appropriate grazing plan, and implement agreed practices. Financial support may depend on separate partner or cost-share eligibility.
records.practice: Managed rotational grazing
records.strategies: Assistance may include grazing planning, fencing, livestock-water systems, stream protection, pasture improvement, producer education, and connections to implementation funding.
records.notes: Nonprofit-administered and often supported with mixed public-private funding. Farmers should ask specifically which planning, equipment, or implementation costs are currently covered.

records.name: Wetlands Watch / Virginia Outdoors Foundation — Coastal Resilience & Trees Fund
records.problem: Provides grants to localities, organizations, community groups, and landowners for wetland restoration, conservation projects, and tree canopy in Virginia’s Coastal Zone.
records.practice: shoreline protection, green infrastructure, tree planting, and stewardship
records.strategies: Prior funding rounds listed individual awards generally up to $5,000–$25,000 depending on project category.

records.name: Farmers for Soil Health
records.problem: Bare soil, erosion, nutrient loss, weak soil structure, low water infiltration and reduced resilience to drought or heavy rainfall
records.agency: Farmers for Soil Health; National Fish and Wildlife Foundation
records.eligibility: Farmer must enroll eligible agricultural acreage in a participating state. Current program materials state that payments are available for planting cover crops on up to 2,000 acres.
records.requirements: Participant must plant the enrolled cover crop, comply with the enrollment contract and provide required acreage and practice documentation. Contracts may be renewed annually during the program period.
records.practice: Cover crop establishment
records.strategies: Current national program materials state an incentive of $35 per acre per year. The approved crop, planting window and seeding specifications should be confirmed during enrollment.
records.notes: Confirm that enrollment is open in the farmer's state and county before planning around the payment. Do not begin solely on the assumption that an application will be approved.

records.name: Healthy Land and Waters Grant
records.problem: Soil erosion, nutrient runoff, reduced soil health and declining water quality
records.eligibility: Farmer or working-land owner must have land within a defined focal area based on watersheds of high conservation importance. Assistance depends on available funding and project fit.
records.requirements: Applicant must work with New Jersey Audubon on project assessment and implementation. The funded practice must support soil health, water quality or wildlife habitat.
records.practice: Cover crop establishment
records.strategies: A documented New Jersey Audubon example used rye and tillage radish. Species and seed mixes are project-specific and should be approved before purchase.
records.notes: Financial assistance is not advertised as universally available across New Jersey; land location within an active focal area is important.

records.name: Healthy Land and Waters Grant
records.problem: Compacted or degraded soil, erosion and poor infiltration
records.eligibility: Farmer or working-land owner must have land within a defined focal area based on watersheds of high conservation importance. Assistance depends on available funding and project fit.
records.requirements: Applicant must coordinate with New Jersey Audubon and implement the approved conservation practice.
records.practice: No-till planting
records.notes: Ask whether the program can cover equipment access, contractor services or only direct practice materials.

records.name: Healthy Land and Waters Grant
records.problem: Habitat loss, reduced biodiversity and degraded working lands
records.eligibility: Farmer or working-land owner must have land within a defined focal area based on watersheds of high conservation importance. Assistance depends on available funding and project fit.
records.requirements: Applicant must coordinate with New Jersey Audubon and implement the approved restoration practice.
records.practice: Wildlife habitat enhancement
records.notes: Funding may prioritize practices that produce both water-quality and habitat benefits.

records.name: Agricultural Conservation Assistance
records.scopeDetail: Maryland; Virginia; Chesapeake Bay watershed project areas
records.problem: Nutrient and sediment runoff, stream degradation, manure impacts and erosion
records.eligibility: Farm must be located within an active Alliance project area, watershed or participating agricultural supply chain. Eligibility and cost share vary by project.
records.requirements: Farmer must work with Alliance staff or project partners on conservation planning and install the approved practice according to applicable technical standards. Maintenance and verification may be required.
records.practice: Riparian forest buffer
records.strategies: Buffer width, planting density, eligible species, livestock exclusion and maintenance requirements depend on the active project and site plan.
records.notes: Ask the Alliance which active project covers the farm. Some projects offer very high cost share, but rates are not uniform across the watershed.

records.name: Chesapeake Bay Farm Stewardship and Preservation
records.problem: Bare soil, erosion, nutrient runoff and declining soil health
records.eligibility: The documented project served participating farmers in Delaware, Maryland and Virginia through project partners.
records.requirements: Participants worked through project partners and complied with the applicable conservation practice requirements.
records.practice: Cover crop establishment
records.notes: The project is marked closed. Verify whether a replacement project is enrolling farmers.

records.name: Regenerative Farm and Food Business Loans
records.problem: Insufficient capital for regenerative transition, soil improvements, water systems or resilient farm infrastructure
records.eligibility: Small- or mid-scale farm or food business committed to regenerative practices. Foodshed Capital states that it prioritizes soil-based, polyculture operations, local or regional sales and borrowers underserved by traditional finance.
records.requirements: Borrower must complete underwriting, use funds for the approved business purpose and repay the loan under the agreed terms.
records.practice: Soil-health infrastructure financing
records.notes: This is a loan, not a grant. Confirm that the farm's state is currently within the lending service area and ask about rates, term, collateral and repayment flexibility.

records.name: Regenerative Agriculture Loans
records.problem: Lack of capital for regenerative land management, resilient infrastructure and farm viability
records.eligibility: Regenerative farm, ranch, fishery or local food business with a viable project, relevant operating capacity and ability to repay.
records.requirements: Borrower must complete underwriting, use loan proceeds for the approved purpose and repay principal and interest.
records.practice: Farm infrastructure financing
records.notes: This is debt financing, not a grant. Ask for the full interest rate, fees, collateral requirements and repayment schedule before applying.

records.name: Coastal Wetland and American Black Duck Habitat Assistance
records.scopeDetail: New Jersey; eligible coastal and wetland project areas
records.problem: Saltwater inundation, tidal wetland degradation, invasive vegetation and loss of coastal habitat
records.eligibility: Private landowner eligibility and funding depend on property location, habitat value, active project priorities and available funding.
records.requirements: Landowner must coordinate with New Jersey Audubon on project design and implement and maintain the approved habitat practice.
records.practice: Coastal wetland habitat restoration
records.notes: Ask specifically whether financial assistance is currently available for the parcel; general stewardship assistance does not guarantee project funding.

records.name: Coastal Wetland and American Black Duck Habitat Assistance
records.scopeDetail: New Jersey; eligible coastal and wetland project areas
records.problem: Invasive plants expanding after hydrologic or salinity change
records.eligibility: Private landowner eligibility and funding depend on property location, habitat value, active project priorities and available funding.
records.requirements: Invasive-species work must be part of an approved habitat restoration or stewardship project and maintained as required.
records.practice: Invasive plant management
records.notes: Do not assume herbicide, contractor labour or follow-up treatment is covered; obtain a written approved scope and maintenance schedule.

records.name: Expanding Agroforestry Project — Expanding Agroforestry Incentive Payment Program
records.agency: The Nature Conservancy and VA Tech for Mid-Atlantic Region, funded through the USDA’s Advancing Markets for Producers initiative
records.eligibility:
Project must be located in an eligible state; Virginia is eligible.
Applicant must own the land or provide a letter from the landowner supporting the project and confirming a lease for the contract period.
The project must establish new agroforestry acreage.
Minimum project size is generally 5 acres.
The entity receiving payment must be registered with the USDA Farm Service Agency for the project acreage.
Producers who do not yet possess all required FSA documentation may still apply if they are willing to become fully eligible.
Trees and shrubs must be ecologically appropriate and approved by The Nature Conservancy.
records.requirements:
Develop an agroforestry project design and budget with the regional technical-assistance provider.
Follow the applicable NRCS Conservation Practice Standard.
Enter an incentive-payment agreement with The Nature Conservancy.
Complete required USDA, FSA, tax, and program paperwork.
Provide evidence that the planting was installed according to the approved plan and NRCS specifications.
Complete required measurement, monitoring, reporting, and verification activities.
Participate for 18 months or through November 2028, whichever is sooner when the contract is signed.
The same practice on the same acreage cannot also be funded through EQIP, CSP, CRP, or another USDA funding source
records.notes: The current application period is June 30 through August 11, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

records.name: Alley Cropping
records.description: Trees or shrubs are planted in single or multiple rows, with agronomic or horticultural crops or forages produced in the alleys between the rows. The woody plants can provide additional products
records.strategies: Trees or shrubs planted in rows with agronomic, horticultural, or forage crops cultivated between rows; examples include wheat, corn, soybeans, hay, sunflowers, medicinal herbs, black walnut, pecan, nut or fruit trees, and short rotation woody crops combined with forage or row crops
records.swiStrategies: Employ shallow minimum till or no till to reduce soil loss and soil subsidence/oxidation; Plant biomass/fiber crops
records.problem: Surface water runoff and erosion, wind erosion, excess subsurface water, water table depth, nutrient utilization, wildlife habitat

records.name: Amending Soil Properties with Gypsum Products
records.description: Application of gypsum (calcium sulfate dihydrate) products to change the physical and/or chemical properties of soil.
records.strategies: Use of gypsum (calcium sulfate dihydrate) products to improve soil properties; gypsum applied based on soil tests and cation exchange capacity
records.swiStrategies: Use soil additives to control saline levels; Add gypsum to decrease salt or utilize low salt compost or manures; Measure soil conditions and/or conduct soil analysis
records.problem: Aluminum toxicity and degraded soil conditions associated with SWI, including poor water infiltration, poor soil aggregate stability, and dissolved phosphorus in surface and ground water (nutrient runoff)

records.name: Brush Management
records.description: Management or removal of woody, nonherbaceous plants, including invasive and noxious species, to achieve desired vegetation conditions.
records.strategies: Management or removal of woody (nonherbaceous or succulent) plants using mechanical, chemical, burning, or biological methods; may include grazing animals for biological control
records.swiStrategies: Reduce or eliminate invasive species
records.problem: Undesirable woody vegetation, invasive and noxious plants, soil erosion, sediment, water quality degradation, degraded hydrology, reduced forage accessibility, and excessive fuel loads.

records.name: Channel Bed Stabilization
records.description: Measures used to stabilize the bed or bottom of a channel. The practice is used where damaging channel aggradation or degradation is occurring and cannot feasibly be controlled by simpler measures.
records.strategies: Measures used to stabilize the bed or bottom of a channel; may include stabilization structures, vegetation, and sediment management measure
records.swiStrategies: Remove hard boundaries (ex. Dams and culverts) to allow for watershed connectivity, facilitate tidal exchange, and downstream sediment flow; Modify or eliminate ditches to restore natural hydrology
records.problem: Channel bed instability, damaging aggradation or degradation, sediment transport and deposition, altered surface water and groundwater levels in floodplains, riparian areas, and wetlands

records.name: Clearing and Snagging
records.description: Removal of snags, drifts, or other obstructions from natural or improved channels to increase flow capacity and reduce risks to adjacent land or infrastructure.
records.strategies: Removal of specified vegetation along streambanks and selective removal of snags, drifts, trees, brush, and other obstructions from natural or improved streams; disturbed areas restored with vegetation, preferably native vegetation from local sources
records.swiStrategies: Reduce interior ponding (providing corridors for water to flow out of forests); Establish vegetation in areas with current or projected high erosion rates
records.problem: Reduced stream, flow capacity, ponding and flooding, excessive bank erosion, sediment transported to surface water, and debris impacts to infrastructure

records.name: Conservation Cover
records.description: Establishing and maintaining permanent vegetative cover. The practice can reduce erosion and sediment transport, reduce nutrient-related water-quality degradation, provide wildlife and pollinator habitat, and improve soil health.
records.strategies: Establishing and maintaining permanent vegetative cover; may include diverse mixtures of tree, shrub, grass, forb, legume species and native species
records.swiStrategies: Reduce or eliminate invasive species; Establish vegetation in areas with current or projected high erosion rates
records.problem: Sediment transport to surface water, water quality degradation (nutrient runoff), poor soil health, soil compaction, and inadequate wildlife and pollinator habitat

records.name: Conservation Crop Rotation
records.description: A planned sequence of at least two different crops grown on the same land over time.
records.strategies: At least two different crops grown over time; may include high-residue crops (e.g., corn or wheat), low-residue crops (e.g., vegetables or soybeans), forage crops, perennial deep-rooted crops, legumes, grasses, broadleaf crops, and cover crops
records.swiStrategies: Transition to salt tolerant cover crops; Plant perennial grasses in highly saline areas to act as a buffer to crops
records.problem: Saline seeps/salt accumulation in soils, poor soil moisture efficiency, nutrient-related water quality degradation (nutrient runoff), soil erosion, reduced soil health/organic matter, and degraded forage and wildlife habitat

records.name: Constructed Wetland
records.description: An artificial wetland ecosystem with hydrophytic vegetation for biological treatment of water.
records.strategies: Artificial wetland ecosystem with hydrophytic vegetation for biological treatment of water; treats wastewater, contaminated runoff, storm water, and drainage water using wetland plants tolerant to nutrients, salts, pesticides, and other contaminants. Invasive and noxious species are not used.
records.swiStrategies: Reduce or eliminate invasive species; Maintain and restore wetlands
records.problem: Nutrient runoff, poor water quality, drainage water contamination, and degraded wetland/waterflow conditions

records.name: Contour Buffer Strips
records.description: Narrow strips of permanent herbaceous vegetative cover established around the hillslope and alternated downslope with wider cropped strips farmed on the contour.
records.strategies: Perennial grass strips alternated with cultivated contour-farmed strips; vegetation consists of adapted grasses or mixtures of grasses and legumes
records.swiStrategies: Install filter strips to remove contaminants from overland flow; Plant perennial grasses in highly saline areas to act as a buffer to crops
records.problem: Soil erosion, sediment transport, nutrient and pesticide runoff, water quality degradation, and poor water infiltration

records.name: Cover Crop
records.description: Grasses, legumes, and other forbs planted for seasonal vegetative cover.
records.strategies: Grasses, legumes, and other forbs planted for seasonal vegetative cover
records.swiStrategies: Transition to salt tolerant cover crops
records.problem: Soil erosion, reduced soil organic matter, poor soil aggregate stability, nutrient-related water quality degradation (nutrient runoff), poor moisture management, and soil compaction

records.name: Critical Area Planting
records.description: Establishing permanent vegetation on sites with high or expected high erosion rates or where physical, chemical, or biological conditions prevent establishment using normal planting methods.
records.strategies: Permanent vegetation establishes on critical erosion areas using adapted grasses, trees, shrubs and vines
records.swiStrategies: Establish vegetation in areas with current or projected high erosion rates
records.problem: High soil erosion rates, unstable streambanks and shorelines, degraded riparian areas, and disturbed or degraded lands

records.name: Deep Tillage
records.description: Performing tillage operations below the normal tillage depth to modify adverse physical or chemical properties of a soil.
records.strategies: Deep tillage below normal tillage depth to fracture restrictive soil layers or mix overwash and deposited materials in the root zone
records.problem: Soil compaction, restrictive soil layers, flood overwash deposits, and adverse soil physical or chemical conditions

records.name: Dike and Levee
records.description: A barrier used to retain water on the landscape using a wetland dike, or to exclude water from the landscape and protect property and infrastructure from flooding using a flood control levee
records.strategies: Wetland dikes or flood control levees used to retain or exclude water from the landscape
records.swiStrategies: Install saltwater intrusion control barriers/devices; Utilize backflow prevention valves on any stormwater or irrigation outfall pipes to prevent/reduce saltwater intrustion
records.problem: Flooding risk, uncontrolled water levels, and water management needs in coastal or low-lying areas

records.name: Diversion
records.description: A channel usually constructed across the slope with a supporting ridge on the lower side
records.strategies: Channels constructed across slopes with a supporting ridge used to intercept, collect, redirect, store, or safely dispose of excess surface and shallow subsurface water; channels are commonly vegetated and may use gravel, concrete, or similar lining materials for erosion protection
records.swiStrategies: Modify or eliminate ditches to restore natural hydrology; Reduce interior ponding (providing corridors for water to flow out of forests); Create off-line storage/harvest of freshwater (retention basin)
records.problem: Surface runoff, erosion, sediment accumulation, seepage problems, and water management issues in sloping or disturbed areas

records.name: Drainage Water Management
records.description: The process of managing water discharges from surface and/or subsurface agricultural drainage systems.
records.strategies: Management of drainage volume and water table elevation by regulating flow from surface or subsurface agricultural drainage systems
records.swiStrategies: Monitor water levels using sensors to establish changes in water levels; Modify or eliminate ditches to restore natural hydrology
records.problem: Poor drainage control, nutrient, pathogen, and pesticide loading, high water tables, poor soil moisture management, and oxidation of organic soils

records.name: Early Successional Habitat Development/Management
records.description: Management of plant succession to develop and maintain early successional habitat to benefit desired wildlife and/or natural communities.
records.strategies: Management of plant succession to develop and maintain early successional habitat for wildlife and natural communities
records.swiStrategies: Reduce or eliminate invasive species
records.problem: Loss of early successional habitat and reduced wildlife habitat diversity

records.name: Field Border
records.description: A strip of permanent vegetation established at the edge or around the perimeter of a field.
records.strategies: Permanent strips of grasses, legumes, forbs, and/or shrubs
records.swiStrategies: Install field borders
records.problem: Erosion, sediment transport, nutrient runoff and degraded water quality

records.name: Field Operations Emissions Reduction
records.description: Adjusting field operations and technologies to reduce emissions from agricultural field operations.
records.strategies: Adjustment of field operations and technologies to reduce particulate matter and nitrogen oxide emissions
records.problem: Particulate matter emissions, wind erosion, and air quality impacts from cropland field operations

records.name: Filter Strip
records.description:
A strip or area of herbaceous vegetation, located at the lower edge(s) of a field, that removes
contaminants from overland flow.
records.strategies: Permanent strips of herbaceous vegetation ( e.g. grasses, legumes)
records.swiStrategies: Install filter strips to remove contaminants from overland flow; Establish vegetation in areas with current or projected high erosion rates
records.problem: Sediment transport, nutrient and contaminant runoff and degraded water quality from overland flow

records.name: Forage Harvest Management
records.description: Timely cutting and removal of forages as hay, green-chop, or ensilage.
records.strategies: Timely cutting and removal of forage crops (e.g. grasses, legumes) as hay, silage or green-chop
records.problem: Nutrient imbalances, soil compaction, reduced forage quality, and pest pressure from poorly timed or excessive forage removal

records.name: Forest Farming
records.description: Establishing or managing trees and shrubs to provide an understory favorable to the production of selected crops.
records.strategies: Managing or establishing stands of trees or shrubs with compatible understory crops or nontimber forest products (e.g. foliage, mushrooms, berries, roots, nuts, etc.)
records.problem: Reduced plant/tree community diversity, low soil organic matter and degraded terrestrial habitat

records.name: Forest Stand Improvement
records.description: Manipulation of tree and shrub species composition, structure, or density to achieve desired forest conditions.
records.strategies: Manipulation of tree and shrub species composition, structure, or density to achieve desired forest conditions
records.swiStrategies: Reduce or eliminate invasive species
records.problem: Poor forest health and productivity, undesirable forest structure and composition,forest pest pressure, wildfire hazard, moisture stress, runoff and erosion risks and inefficient precipitation management

records.name: Forest Trails and Landings
records.description: A temporary or infrequently used route, path, or cleared area used for forest management purposes.
records.strategies: Establishing and managing forest trails and landings; locating routes to minimize soil, water, and habitat impacts; providing adequate drainage; stabilizing disturbed areas; controlling erosion and runoff; and closing or rehabilitating trails and landings when no longer needed.
records.problem: Soil erosion, soil rutting, compaction, hydrologic disturbance, water quality degradation, stream and riparian damage, and habitat fragmentation caused by unmanaged forest access routes

records.name: Grassed Waterway
records.description:
A shaped or graded channel that is established with suitable vegetation to convey surface water at a
nonerosive velocity using a broad and shallow cross section to a stable outlet.
records.strategies: Grasses, tall bunch grasses, perennial forbs, legumes, and flowering plants used for runoff stabilization and habitat improvement
records.swiStrategies: Establish vegetation in areas with current or projected high erosion rates
records.problem: Concentrated surface runoff, gully formation, soil erosion, sediment transport, flooding, and degraded downstream water quality

records.name: Hedgerow Planting
records.description: Establishment of dense perennial vegetation in a linear design to achieve a conservation purpose.
records.strategies: Dense perennial linear plantings of woody plants, shrubs, trees, bunch grasses, and pollinator-supporting vegetation
records.swiStrategies: Establish vegetation in areas with current or projected high erosion rates
records.problem: Habitat fragmentation, airborne dust, chemical drift, odor movement, limited wildlife habitat, and reduced carbon storage

records.name: Mulching
records.description: Applying plant residues or other suitable materials to the land surface.
records.strategies: Application of plant residues, grain straw, grass hay, wood chips, bark, shavings, gravel, synthetic mulch, or other suitable materials to the soil surface
records.problem: Soil erosion, high runoff, soil moisture loss, inefficient irrigation water use, bank erosion, declining soil organic matter and reduced plant productivity

records.name: Nutrient Management
records.description: Managing the rate, source, placement, and timing of plant nutrients and soil amendments while reducing environmental impacts.
records.strategies: Management of nutrient source, rate, timing, and placement for fertilizers, manure, compost, biosolids, crop residues, irrigation water, and other nutrient sources
records.swiStrategies: Measure soil conditions and/or conduct soil analysis
records.problem: Excess nutrients in surface and groundwater, nutrient losses through runoff or leaching, reduced soil organic matter, nutrient imbalances

records.name: Open Channel
records.description:
A natural or artificial conduit in which water flows with a free surface at
atmospheric pressure.
records.strategies: Construction, improvement or restoration of natural or artificial open channels for water conveyance
records.swiStrategies: Modify or eliminate ditches to restore natural hydrology; Reduce interior ponding (providing corridors for water to flow out of forests)
records.problem: Flooding, drainage limitations, water management needs, and protection or enhancement of wildlife habitat

records.name: Pasture and Hay Planting
records.description:
Establishing adapted and compatible species, varieties, or cultivars of perennial herbaceous plants
suitable for pasture or hay production
records.strategies: Perennial herbaceous plants, including cool-season and warm-season grasses, legumes, and broadleaf forage species
records.swiStrategies: Plant perennial grasses in highly saline areas to act as a buffer to crops
records.problem: Reduced forage supply, poor livestock nutrition and health, soil erosion, degraded water quality, degraded air quality, and poor soil health

records.name: Pond
records.description:
A water impoundment made by constructing an embankment, excavating a dugout, or a combination of
both.
records.strategies: Water impoundments constructed as embankment ponds, excavated ponds, or a combination of both for water storage and managemen
records.swiStrategies: Create off-line storage/harvest of freshwater (retention basin)
records.problem: Need for water storage,erosion control, flow detention and water quality improvement

records.name: Prescribed Burning
records.description: Planned fire applied to a predetermined area.
records.strategies: Planned fire applied to a predetermined area
records.swiStrategies: Reduce or eliminate invasive species
records.problem: Undesirable vegetation, pest, pathogen and disease pressure, wildfire hazards from biomass accumulation, degraded wildlife habitat, reduced plant productivity, forage imbalance, and poor soil health

records.name: Prescribed Grazing
records.description:
Managing vegetation with grazing and browsing animals to achieve specific ecological,
economic, and management objectives
records.strategies: Management of vegetation with grazing and browsing animals
records.swiStrategies: Reduce or eliminate invasive species
records.problem: Poor forage quantity and quality, sediment and nutrient transport, runoff, soil compaction, groundwater depletion, poor soil health, soil erosion, degraded wildlife habitat, wildfire fuel accumulation, and invasive plant pressure

records.name: Recreation Land Improvement and Protection
records.description: Recreation land grading and shaping is reshaping the surface of the land to support recreational land use.
records.strategies: Land grading, shaping, drainage improvements, and establishment of vegetation to support recreational land use; may include grasses, forbs, trees, and shrubs adapted to site conditions
records.swiStrategies: Establish vegetation in areas with current or projected high erosion rates
records.problem: Surface irregularities, slopes, obstructions, or drainage limitations that interfere with planned recreational use; resource damage from recreational land use

records.name: Residue and Tillage Management, No-Till
records.description: Limiting soil disturbance to manage the amount, orientation, and distribution of crop and plant residue on the soil surface year aroun
records.strategies: Limiting soil disturbance; eliminating full-width soil disturbance between cash crops; uniformly distributing crop residues across the field; maintaining sufficient surface residue to control erosion; and maintaining year-round residue cover where applicable
records.swiStrategies: Employ shallow minimum till or no till to reduce soil loss and soil subsidence/oxidation
records.problem: Sheet, rill and wind erosion; excessive sediment in surface waters; tillage-induced particulate emissions; low soil organic matter and poor aggregate stability; low plant-available moisture; high energy use; and limited wildlife food and escape cover

records.name: Residue and Tillage Management, Reduced Till
records.description: Managing the amount, orientation, and distribution of crops and other plant residue on the soil surface year-round while limiting soil-disturbing activities used to grow and harvest crops in systems where the field surface is tilled prior to planting.
records.strategies: Reducing the intensity and frequency of tillage; using mulch tillage, conservation tillage, ridge tillage, or other reduced-tillage systems; uniformly distributing crop residues across the field; maintaining sufficient surface residue to reduce erosion; and avoiding primary inversion tillage
records.swiStrategies: Employ shallow minimum till or no till to reduce soil loss and soil subsidence/oxidation
records.problem: Sheet, rill and wind erosion; excessive sediment in surface waters; tillage-induced particulate emissions; low soil organic matter and poor aggregate stability; low plant-available moisture; high energy use; and limited wildlife food and escape cover

records.name: Restoration of Rare or Declining Natural Communities
records.description:
Reestablishment of abiotic (physical and chemical) and biotic (biological) conditions necessary to support
rare or declining natural assemblages of native plants and animals
records.strategies: Restore physical/environmental conditions needed by rare or declining natural communities; replace or add substrate; install natural structural elements; create topographic features or chemical conditions that support restoration of native plant communitie
records.swiStrategies: Maintain and restore wetlands; Modify or eliminate ditches to restore natural hydrology; Reduce or eliminate invasive species; Where salinization has impacted the soil past the point of farming, transition to tidal saltmarsh
records.problem: Degraded plant condition; inadequate wildlife habitat; degradation or loss of rare or declining native natural communities.

records.name: Riparian Forest Buffer
records.description: An area predominantly covered by trees and/or shrubs located adjacent to and up-gradient from a watercourse or water body.
records.strategies: Existing, naturally regenerated, or planted native, noninvasive trees and shrubs adapted to site soil and hydrologic conditions; species may provide timber, nuts, fruit, florals, browse, nesting habitat, and aesthetic value
records.swiStrategies: Install riparian buffers in the transitional zone between upland and aquatic habitats to trap sediments and filter pollutants; Reduce or eliminate invasive species
records.problem: Sediment transport, nutrient transport, pathogen, pesticide and chemical movement to surface and groundwater, degraded riparian habitat, elevated stream temperatures, reduced carbon storage, and degraded riparian plant communities

records.name: Riparian Herbaceous Cover
records.description: Grasses, sedges, rushes, ferns, legumes, and forbs tolerant of intermittent flooding or saturated soils established or managed as the dominant vegetation in the transitional zone between upland and aquatic habitats.
records.strategies: Establishment or management of grasses, sedges, rushes, ferns, legumes, and forbs tolerant of intermittent flooding or saturated soils as the dominant vegetation between upland and aquatic habitats
records.swiStrategies: Install riparian buffers in the transitional zone between upland and aquatic habitats to trap sediments and filter pollutants; Establish vegetation in areas with current or projected high erosion rates
records.problem: Degraded water quality, sediment transport, streambank erosion, loss of riparian habitat, reduced floodplain water storage, loss of pollinator habitat, and disturbed riparian plant communities

records.name: Saline and Sodic Soil Management
records.description:
Management of land, water, and plants to reduce the accumulation impacts of salts, sodium, or
combination of salts and sodium on the soil surface and in the rooting zone
records.strategies: Salinity mapping (EC); leaching of salts; salt-tolerant vegetation; salt-tolerant cover crops with fibrous roots; deep-rooted, long-season, or perennial species in saline seep recharge areas; gypsum or other calcium amendments; subsoiling; surface or subsurface drainage; revegetation of saline seep discharge areas with species adapted to excess soil moisture
records.swiStrategies: Use soil additives to control saline levels; Add gypsum to decrease salt or utilize low salt compost or manures; Measure soil conditions and/or conduct soil analysis; Plant perennial grasses in highly saline areas to act as a buffer to crops
records.problem: Salt accumulation in the root zone, salt toxicity limiting plant growth, soil crusting, reduced permeability, poor soil aggregate stability, saline seep recharge and discharge areas, wind erosion from sparsely vegetated saline or sodic soils

records.name: Saturated Buffer
records.description: A subsurface, perforated distribution pipe used to reduce the concentration of nitrate in agricultural drainage water diverted beneath a vegetated buffer along its length and discharge channel.
records.strategies: Vegetated riparian buffer with artificially raised water table; minimum 30-ft buffer width; vigorously growing herbaceous vegetation, woody shrubs, trees, or a combination; perforated distribution line installed parallel to the watercourse; water control structure used to divert drainage water into the buffer
records.swiStrategies: Install riparian buffers in the transitional zone between upland and aquatic habitats to trap sediments and filter pollutants; Maintain and restore wetlands; Monitor water levels using sensors to establish changes in water levels
records.problem: Elevated nitrate loading in drainage water; altered wetland hydrology; excess drainage discharge to surface waters

records.name: Seasonal Water Management for Wildlife
records.description: The seasonal inundation of lands with water to provide specific life cycle needs for fish or wildlife.
records.strategies: Seasonal inundation using dikes, ditches, pumps, flooding, or water control structures; management of water depth, duration, timing, and drawdown; habitat for shorebirds, waterfowl, wading birds, mammals, fish, reptiles, and amphibians
records.swiStrategies: Maintain and restore wetlands
records.problem: Loss of wetland habitat, altered hydrology, lack of seasonal standing water for wildlife, need for refuge habitat during flooding events

records.name: Silvopasture
records.description: Establishment and/or management of desired trees and forages on the same land unit.
records.strategies: Establishment and management of trees, forages, and optionally shrubs on the same acreage; trees may be planted in rows, clumps, or as single trees; forage species compatible with livestock and tree species; diverse seed mixes including native forbs and legumes may be used
records.problem: Reduced forage productivity, livestock heat or weather stress, soil erosion, degraded water quality, reduced wildlife habitat, low biological diversity, poor soil quality

records.name: Soil Carbon Amendment
records.description: Application of carbon-based amendments derived from plant materials or treated animal byproducts.
records.strategies: Application of compost, biochar, and other carbon-based materials derived from plant materials or treated animal byproducts
records.swiStrategies: Use soil additives to control saline levels
records.problem: Poor soil organic matter, poor soil aggregate stability, degraded soil health, reduced soil biological activity, low carbon storage

records.name: Stream Habitat Improvement and Management
records.description: Improve, restore, or maintain the ecological functions of a stream and its adjacent floodplain and riparian area
records.strategies: Stream habitat assessment; floodplain and wetland connectivity improvements; riparian vegetation restoration using native plants; aquatic organism passage; backwater and off-channel habitat creation; large wood placement, spawning riffles, boulder complexes, and riparian buffer establishment
records.swiStrategies: Remove hard boundaries (ex. Dams and culverts) to allow for watershed connectivity, facilitate tidal exchange, and downstream sediment flow; Reduce or eliminate invasive species; Install riparian buffers in the transitional zone between upland and aquatic habitats to trap sediments and filter pollutants; Maintain and restore wetlands
records.problem: Impaired stream habitat, degraded riparian areas, reduced floodplain connectivity, poor aquatic habitat conditions, altered stream function

records.name: Streambank and Shoreline Protection
records.description:
Treatment(s) used to stabilize and protect banks of streams or constructed channels and shorelines of
lakes, reservoirs, or estuaries.
records.strategies: Vegetative or structural measures to stabilize and protect streambanks, shorelines, estuaries, lakes, reservoirs, or excavated channels from scour and erosion; may include revegetation, native grasses, forbs, legumes, shrubs, trees, riprap, gabions, buffer establishment, toe protection, and livestock exclusion
records.swiStrategies: Develop living shorelines to reduce erosion and marsh loss; Install streambank and shoreline protection measures; Establish vegetation in areas with current or projected high erosion rates
records.problem: Streambank erosion, shoreline erosion, land loss, sediment delivery to downstream waters, degraded riparian habitat, unstable banks, scour of estuarine and stream shorelines

records.name: Stripcropping
records.description: Planned rotations of crops in systematic arrangement of alternating strips across a field.
records.strategies: Planned rotation of erosion-resistant and erosion-susceptible crops arranged in alternating strips; may include crops, forages, specialty crops, cover crops, and grass/legume forage crops; strips are laid out across slopes or perpendicular to prevailing erosive winds
records.problem: Soil erosion, sediment transport to surface waters, nutrient runoff, pesticide transport, wind erosion, reduced infiltration

records.name: Subsurface Drain
records.strategies: Subsurface drainage pipes or conduit systems installed below ground to remove or distribute soil water; may include drainage laterals, outlets, filters, envelopes, water control structures, sediment traps, and drainage water management components
records.swiStrategies: Modify or eliminate ditches to restore natural hydrology; Perform hydrologic interventions (e.g., creation of aquifer recharge/salinity intrusion recharge wells/French drains to distribute freshwater to aquifer and protect freshwater lens)
records.problem: Shallow water table, saturated soils, ponding, flooding, poor plant health and productivity, poor field trafficability, accumulation of salts in the root zone, livestock stress associated with excessive soil moisture

records.name: Surface Drain, Field Ditch
records.strategies: Graded field ditch designed to intercept, collect, and convey excess surface water, shallow subsurface water, seepage, or irrigation water to a stable outlet; may be used with drainage water management, riparian buffers, filter strips, and fencing
records.problem: Ponding, flooding, excess surface water, shallow subsurface water, poor field drainage, poor trafficability, salt accumulation associated with poor drainage

records.name: Surface Drain, Main or Lateral
records.strategies: Open drainage ditch constructed to a designed size and grade that receives drainage water from field ditches and subsurface drains and conveys it to a safe outlet
records.problem: Ponding, flooding, excess surface water, shallow subsurface water, poor drainage, waterlogged soils

records.name: Surface Roughening
records.strategies: Emergency tillage operations that create random soil surface roughness (clods, ridges, rough soil surface) to reduce wind erosion; may include chiseling, skip chiseling, deep tillage, lister/bedder operations, or ridging perpendicular to prevailing winds
records.problem: Wind erosion, wind-blown sediment, bare or sparsely covered soils, soil particle abrasion of crops, airborne dust

records.name: Trails and Walkways
records.strategies: Constructed path with a vegetated, earthen, gravel, paved, or other hardened surface to facilitate movement of animals, people, or off-road vehicles; may include vegetated trails, gravel walkways, hardened surfaces, elevated walkways, drainage structures, fencing, gates, bridges, and erosion-control measures
records.problem: Soil compaction and erosion caused by concentrated animal, pedestrian, or vehicle traffic; damage to sensitive or wet areas; degraded access to forage, water, shelter, or management areas

records.name: Tree/Shrub Establishment
records.strategies: Establishment of trees and shrubs through planting seedlings or cuttings, seeding, or promoting natural regeneration; species selection, planting method, spacing, and site preparation vary according to site conditions and management objectives
records.problem: Loss of desirable vegetation, erosion, degraded wildlife habitat, degraded water quality, need for forest cover establishment

records.name: Tree/Shrub Pruning
records.strategies: Removal of selected branches, leaders, or roots from trees and shrubs to improve plant health, vigor, structure, understory conditions, or reduce wildfire hazards; may include crown pruning, root pruning, ladder fuel reduction, and removal of diseased branches
records.problem: Poor tree or shrub health, excessive pest pressure, dense canopy limiting understory growth, wildfire hazards, undesirable plant structure, reduced understory vigor

records.name: Tree/Shrub Site Preparation
records.strategies: Site preparation using mechanical treatments, herbicides, prescribed burning, vegetation management, residue management, soil preparation, mineral soil exposure, compaction alleviation, and temporary water management to improve establishment of desired trees and shrubs
records.problem: Poor tree/shrub establishment, competing vegetation, pest and disease pressure, flooding or seasonally high water that limits woody plant establishment, degraded sites requiring revegetation

records.name: Upland Wildlife Habitat Management
records.strategies: Vegetation establishment for shelter, food, and movement; structural measures to provide shelter, food, or movement; vegetation management to sustain habitat conditions over tim
records.problem: Degraded wildlife habitat, habitat fragmentation, lack of shelter, cover, food resources, or habitat connectivity for wildlife

records.name: Vegetated Treatment Area
records.strategies: Permanent vegetation used to treat agricultural wastewater; may include grasses, legumes, and other forbs adapted to site conditions; wastewater applied as sheet flow across a vegetated area for nutrient and contaminant removal
records.problem: Nutrient runoff, contaminated agricultural runoff, degraded surface water quality, pathogen transport, agricultural wastewater discharge

records.name: Vegetative Barrier
records.strategies: Permanent strips of stiff, dense vegetation established along contours or across concentrated flow areas; vegetation must be adapted to local soil and climate conditions, long-lived, manageable, and capable of maintaining dense, upright stems; may be established from seed or vegetative material
records.problem: Sheet and rill erosion, ephemeral gully erosion, sediment transport to surface waters

records.name: Wetland Creation
records.strategies: Creation of a wetland on a site that was historically not a wetland; establishment of wetland hydrology through shallow inundation or soil saturation; may include wetland vegetation established by natural colonization, seeding, or planting; may include native wetland plant communities, herbaceous vegetation, shrubs, and trees adapted to anaerobic conditions
records.swiStrategies: Maintain and restore wetlands
records.problem: Frequent flooding, loss of wetland habitat, poor water quality, loss of native wetland vegetation, conversion of uplands to wetland conditions due to changing hydrology

records.name: Wetland Enhancement
records.strategies: Enhancement of existing wetlands through hydrology management, hydric soil improvements, vegetation enhancement, invasive species removal, seeding or planting desired wetland species, water control structures, microtopography or macrotopography modifications, and habitat improvements
records.swiStrategies: Modify or eliminate ditches to restore natural hydrology; Reduce or eliminate invasive species; Install riparian buffers in the transitional zone between upland and aquatic habitats to trap sediments and filter pollutants; Maintain and restore wetlands
records.problem: Degraded wetlands, loss of wetland habitat, altered hydrology, invasive species, reduced native wetland vegetation, reduced fish and wildlife habitat

records.name: Wetland Restoration
records.strategies: Re-establishment of wetland hydrology, topography, and substrate to approximate historic wetland conditions; may include removal of fill, breaking or removing drainage tile, replacing perforated tile with solid tile, breaching berms or levees, filling pits or ponds, grading to restore microtopography, and installing water control structures
records.swiStrategies: Maintain and restore wetlands; modify or eliminate ditches to restore natural hydrology; remove hard boundaries (ex. Dams and culverts) to allow for watershed connectivity, facilitate tidal exchange, and downstream sediment flow
records.problem: Loss of wetlands, altered hydrology, drainage of wetlands, wetland degradation, loss of wetland habitat, reduced water quality, changes in wetland vegetation

records.name: Wetland Wildlife Habitat Management
records.strategies: Management of wetland habitat through native plant establishment, invasive species control, water level management, vegetative buffers, artificial nesting structures, snags, logs, tree trunks, and other habitat features that support wetland-dependent wildlif
records.problem: Loss of wetland habitat, reduced habitat quality for wetland-dependent wildlife, habitat fragmentation, invasive species, lack of nesting, feeding, or cover habitat

records.name: Wildlife Habitat Planting
records.strategies: Establishment of wildlife habitat through planting herbaceous vegetation and/or shrubs; may include native grasses, forbs, shrubs, pollinator habitat plantings, and plant communities designed to resemble historic native vegetation
records.problem: Degraded wildlife habitat, low plant diversity, poor pollinator habitat, lack of food and cover for wildlife, conversion of cropland or pastureland to habitat

records.name: Windbreak/Shelterbelt Establishment and Renovation
records.strategies: Single or multiple rows of trees and/or shrubs established, enhanced, or renovated in linear or curvilinear configurations
records.problem: Wind erosion, wind damage to plants, ponding and flooding associated with snow accumulation, poor moisture management, livestock exposure to wind and heat, air quality concerns

records.name: Woody Residue Treatment
records.strategies: Treatment of residual woody material through chipping, mastication, crushing, compacting, lop and scatter, piling, burning, or offsite removal; adequate woody material is retained to support nutrient cycling, soil protection, and soil organic matter
records.problem: Excess woody debris, hazardous fuel accumulation, insect and disease risks, restricted access for management activities, reduced forage access, impaired regeneration of plant communities

records.name: Herbaceous Weed Treatment
records.strategies: Removal or control of herbaceous weeds using mechanical, chemical, biological, or integrated methods; may include mowing, manual removal, targeted grazing, herbicides, or spot-flaming
records.problem: Invasive, noxious, prohibited, or undesirable herbaceous plants; reduced forage quality; degraded wildlife habitat; erosion concerns; excessive fine fuels and wildfire hazard

records.name: Irrigation Field Ditch
records.strategies: Permanent earthen irrigation ditch used to convey water from a water source to one or more irrigated fields; may include vegetative cover on ditch banks and associated water-control structures
records.problem: Inefficient irrigation water delivery, poor water distribution, water losses during irrigation

records.name: Structure for Water Control
records.strategies: Permanent water-control structures including flashboard risers, water level control structures, check dams, checks, head gates, pipe drop inlets, box inlets, tide gates, water management gates, culverts, chutes, and water measurement devices
records.swiStrategies: Install saltwater intrusion control barriers/devices; utilize backflow prevention valves on any stormwater or irrigation outfall pipes to prevent/reduce saltwater intrustion; install salinity control barriers on tax ditches
records.problem: Poor water-level management, flooding, drainage issues, water table management needs, wetland hydrology restoration, tidal backflow, saltwater movement through drainage systems

records.name: Water and Sediment Control Basin (WASCOB)
records.strategies: Earth embankment or combination ridge and channel constructed across the slope of a minor drainageway; basin may use an underground outlet, pipe drop structure, soil infiltration area, stable channel, or combination of outlet types; nonfarmed disturbed areas are vegetated with permanent native or noninvasive vegetation
records.problem: Gully erosion; sediment transport and deposition; excessive runoff; runoff and sediment damage to land and improvements

records.name: Contour Farming
records.strategies: Aligning ridges, furrows, and roughness formed by tillage, planting, and other operations at a grade near the contour to alter the velocity or direction of water flow
records.problem: Sheet and rill erosion; sediment transport to surface waters; excess nutrients in surface waters; pesticide transport to surface waters; inefficient moisture management

records.name: Contour Orchard and Other Perennial Crops
records.strategies: Planting orchards, vineyards, or other perennial crops so field operations are performed on or near the contour; vegetative ground cover may be maintained in alleys, row furrows, terraces, and diversions to increase infiltration, reduce runoff, and control erosion
records.problem: Sheet and rill soil erosion; sediment transport to surface waters; poor water infiltration

records.name: Cross Wind Ridges
records.strategies: Ridges formed by tillage, planting, or other operations and aligned perpendicular to prevailing wind direction during critical wind erosion periods; ridges may be established using chisel plows, drills with hoe openers, or other implements that form effective ridges
records.problem: Wind erosion; reduced plant productivity and health; particulate matter emissions

records.name: Dam
records.strategies: Artificial barrier used to impound water; may provide flood-control storage and permanent water storage for beneficial uses such as irrigation or livestock supply; may include shallow reservoir areas and wetland habitat for wildlife
records.problem: Downstream flood damage; insufficient water storage; degraded fish and wildlife habitat

records.name: Precision Land Forming and Smoothing
records.strategies: Regrading fields to remove depressions, mounds, old terraces, turnrows, and other surface irregularities; developing uniform slopes to allow drainage across the field; balancing cuts and fills; carrying runoff to a stable outlet
records.problem: Poor surface drainage; erosion; surface irregularities that interfere with drainage and equipment operation

excluded.name: Organic and Regenerative Farm Financing
excluded.reason: Funds for purchasing land for regenerative or organic farming- not current land
